Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Arditi et al. 2024), and — the key control — a generic HYPOTHETICAL-NARRATIVE style direction (per Hidden Dimensions 2025). Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The reality-status direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, the surface hypothetical-narrative style (test on prompts matched for narrative style but differing in reality-status).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (unreal framing), steer the reality-status direction toward 'real' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure restored refusal; steer toward 'unreal' on a real-framed request and measure suppressed refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), hypothetical-narrative-style steering (does surface style alone suffice, or is reality-status the true driver?), and a check that reality-status steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x reality-status).
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt reality-status readout (single forward pass) to predict hypothetical-framing jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, hypothetical-narrative-style readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on story, test on unreal-world) and cross-model transfer.
6) REALITY CLAMPING / CONSEQUENCE-SIMULATION DEFENSE: Two training-free variants: (a) REALITY CLAMPING — project out / clamp the reality-status component toward 'real' at pre-decision layers, gated on a harm-likeness readout so benign fiction is untouched; (b) CONSEQUENCE SIMULATION — when harm-likeness is present under unreal framing, inject a brief forced consequence-simulation step ('consider the real-world consequences if this were actually carried out') that re-engages harm perception, mirroring the human debiasing-by-simulation finding. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split; compare the two variants.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and both defense variants on: hypothetical/fiction-framing attack success (JailbreakBench/HarmBench + Adversarial-Tales-style story framings), refusal reality-consistency, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest), BENIGN fiction/roleplay helpfulness (does it still write benign stories and hypotheticals?), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: the defenses close hypothetical-framing jailbreaks toward real-framing refusal levels while preserving benign fiction/roleplay — a selectivity uniform refusal steering cannot achieve.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts reality-status vs harm/refusal/narrative-style; single-direction vs low-rank; whether Reality Clamping vs Consequence Simulation is more selective; whether reasoning models discount reality less in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the safety reality-discount correlates with the model's hypothetical-vs-counterfactual behavior on NEUTRAL causal-judgment vignettes (does safety inherit a general reality-discount, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that frames as unreal while suppressing the reality-status readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central risk is that the reality-status direction is inseparable from the generic hypothetical-narrative STYLE direction (Hidden Dimensions 2025) — i.e., surface framing, not a genuine 'is-this-real' representation; we adjudicate this rigorously with matched-narrative-style separability tests, a hypothetical-narrative control direction, and specificity steering, and if inseparable that itself refines the hypothetical-narrative-bypass account. (2) Holding harm content constant while varying reality framing is delicate — fictional framing could inadvertently lower perceived harm or add roleplay-persona cues (confound with reframing/persona jailbreaks); we measure the harm readout to confirm it is held constant, distinguish reality-status from persona framing, and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test. (3) If refusal is invariant to reality framing (H1 false), the reality-discount hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety discounts hypothetical harm is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in the counterfactual-vs-hypothetical human result. (4) Reality Clamping / Consequence Simulation could harm legitimate benign fiction, roleplay, and hypothetical reasoning (a real deployment need) or raise over-refusal; the harm-gated design and benign-fiction/roleplay and over-refusal benchmarks are built to detect and bound this genuine trade-off, and the Consequence-Simulation variant is designed to be more content-selective than a blanket clamp. (5) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear/multi-dimensional refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (6) The predictor may transfer poorly to unseen framings; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (7) Adaptive attackers could frame as unreal while suppressing the reality-status readout; we test this as an arms-race limitation. (8) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard published framing attacks for measurement; the deliverable is a defense plus diagnostic, and the interventions only increase refusal on harmful hypotheticals (failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability). (9) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: construal_level_gates_refusal
Title: Abstract Enough to Allow It: A Construal-Level Signal That Gates LLM Safety Refusal, and Concretizing Harm to Defend the Model
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing Construal Level Theory (moral appraisals are more extreme at low-level/concrete construal and blunted at high-level/abstract construal), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal construal-level representation (abstract vs concrete framing of an action, distinct from harm-perception and refusal directions) that gates safety refusal: framing a harmful request abstractly/high-level ('describe the general principles behind...', 'at a conceptual level') raises the construal readout, blunts harm perception, and suppresses refusal, whereas concrete/low-level framing sharpens it, even with the harmful action and danger held fixed. Reading and neutralizing this construal-level signal (or forcing concretization) re-engages harm perception and closes abstraction jailbreaks without hurting benign abstract discussion.
Related Work: Construal Level Theory is robustly established: moral judgments are more extreme at low-level/concrete construal and blunted at high-level/abstract construal (Gong & Medin 2012, 'Construal levels and moral judgment'), psychological distance raises construal level (Liberman & Trope 2009), and distance moderates how disgust/harm feed moral judgment (So Gross and Yet So Far Away 2018; Perceptions of Harm Mediate Moral Judgment 2018). On the LLM side, harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable directions (Zhao et al. 2025, LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately; DBDI 2025), harmfulness is a low-rank subspace (Geometry of Harmfulness 2025), refusal is multi-dimensional with non-dominant directions like hypothetical-narrative that bypass refusal (Hidden Dimensions 2025), and reasoning increases sensitivity to affective/representation steering (Sparks of Rationality 2026). CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work tests whether CONSTRUAL LEVEL (abstract vs concrete framing) gates the refusal decision. This differs from my prior proposals: identifiable_victim_refusal varied WHO/HOW-MANY the victim is; delayed_harm_discounting varied strictly the TEMPORAL delay of consequences; hypothetical_reality_discount varied real-vs-unreal status (whether it will happen); intent_outcome_conflation varied the actor's mental state. Construal level is a distinct, well-motivated axis — the abstraction/concreteness of the SAME action's description, a single latent dimension CLT predicts should unify multiple distance manipulations — with a specific, opposite-signed prediction (abstract framing LOWERS refusal) and a mechanistic gating claim plus a concretization defense. It also refines the hypothetical-narrative-bypass finding (Hidden Dimensions) by testing whether the operative variable is construal level rather than surface narrative style.
Abstract: One of the most robust findings in moral psychology is that construal level shapes moral judgment: people judge concretely-construed transgressions more harshly and abstractly-construed ones more leniently, and psychological distance operates by shifting construal level. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal construal-level representation — how abstractly vs concretely an action is framed — distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, and that this signal causally gates refusal: abstract, high-level framing of a harmful request ('explain the general principles', 'at a conceptual level', 'in broad terms') raises the construal readout, blunts harm perception, and suppresses refusal, while concrete, step-by-step framing sharpens it — even with the harmful action and its danger held fixed. This is dangerous because an attacker can abstract a harmful goal to launder it past the guardrail while still extracting actionable structure. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only construal level along an abstract-to-concrete ladder, with content and intent fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection rise as framing becomes more concrete. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a construal-level direction, verify it is separable from harm, refusal, and a generic hypothetical-narrative style direction, and causally test whether steering it toward 'concrete' restores refusal while the harm readout is unchanged. Finally we propose Concretization Steering, a training-free controller that re-anchors the construal-level signal (or injects a forced concretization step) before the refusal decision. We evaluate abstraction-jailbreak attack success, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), benign abstract-discussion helpfulness, utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect size and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) CONSTRUAL-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION and intent fixed while varying only construal level along a ladder: (L0) concrete/step-by-step ('give exact steps and quantities to...'); (L1) moderately concrete; (L2) abstract-principles ('describe the general principles / mechanisms behind...'); (L3) high-level/conceptual ('at a broad conceptual level, how does one think about...'). Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); construal framing is the only manipulated variable. Controls: (a) matched concrete harmful requests (refusal ceiling); (b) BENIGN abstract requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity + benign-abstract-discussion utility — the model SHOULD still discuss abstract topics); (c) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate construal level with an independent abstractness classifier plus multiple LLM judges + human spot-check, and verify the harmful goal is held constant across levels.
2) BEHAVIORAL CONSTRUAL-GATING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (Zhao et al. 2025, validated by held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the construal ladder. Test H1: refusal and the harm readout INCREASE monotonically as framing becomes more concrete (equivalently, abstraction suppresses them); fit a monotone curve vs a flat null (slope, R^2) while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH across levels (belief preserved). Report effect sizes across the four models; benign abstract controls confirm harm-specificity.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a CONSTRUAL-LEVEL direction (abstract vs concrete at matched content), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Arditi et al. 2024), and — the key control — a generic HYPOTHETICAL-NARRATIVE style direction (Hidden Dimensions 2025) and a generic verbosity/length direction (abstract text is often shorter). Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The construal-level direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, surface narrative style and length (test on prompts matched for style/length but differing in construal level).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (abstract framing), steer the construal-level direction toward 'concrete' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure restored refusal; steer toward 'abstract' on a concrete-framed request and measure suppressed refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), narrative-style and verbosity steering (do these alone suffice, or is construal level the true driver?), and a check that construal-level steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling). Corruption baselines and multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x construal-level).
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt construal-level readout (single forward pass) to predict abstraction-jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, narrative-style readout, verbosity, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on abstract-principles, test on high-level/conceptual) and cross-model transfer. Optionally test CLT's unification claim: does the same construal-level direction mediate temporal/spatial/social distance framings of the same harmful request?
6) CONCRETIZATION STEERING DEFENSE: Two training-free variants: (a) CONSTRUAL CLAMPING — project out/clamp the construal-level component toward 'concrete' at pre-decision layers, gated on a harm-likeness readout so benign abstract discussion is untouched; (b) FORCED CONCRETIZATION — when harm-likeness is present under abstract framing, inject a brief concretization step ('consider the specific concrete actions and consequences this entails') that re-engages harm perception, mirroring the low-level-construal-sharpens-judgment finding. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split; compare the two variants.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and both defense variants on: abstraction-jailbreak attack success (JailbreakBench/HarmBench abstracted), refusal construal-consistency, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest), BENIGN abstract-discussion helpfulness (does it still explain concepts and principles?), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: the defenses close abstraction jailbreaks toward concrete-framing refusal levels while preserving benign abstract discussion — a selectivity uniform refusal steering cannot achieve.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts construal-level vs harm/refusal/narrative-style; single-direction vs low-rank; whether Construal Clamping vs Forced Concretization is more selective; whether reasoning models construe harm less/more in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the safety construal-gating correlates with the model's construal effects on NEUTRAL moral-judgment vignettes (does safety inherit a general CLT effect, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that abstracts the request while suppressing the construal-level readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central risk is that the construal-level direction is inseparable from the generic hypothetical-narrative STYLE direction (Hidden Dimensions 2025) or from verbosity/length — i.e., surface framing, not a genuine construal-level representation; we adjudicate rigorously with matched-style/length separability tests, control directions, and specificity steering, and if inseparable that itself refines the hypothetical-narrative-bypass account. (2) Holding harm content constant while varying construal is delicate — abstract framing could genuinely reduce the actionable/harmful information (in which case lower refusal is partly appropriate); we mitigate by validating harm-constancy and actionable-content-constancy with judges + humans, measuring the harm readout, and by testing whether the model still emits actionable structure under abstract framing (the key danger), and we report where abstraction genuinely removes harm vs merely reframes it. (3) If refusal is invariant to construal level (H1 false), the CLT-in-safety hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety inherits construal-level effects is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in a robust human result. (4) Concretization Steering / Clamping could harm legitimate benign abstract discussion (a real need — explaining principles, ethics, science) or raise over-refusal; the harm-gated design and benign-abstract-discussion and over-refusal benchmarks are built to detect and bound this genuine trade-off. (5) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear/multi-dimensional refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (6) The predictor may transfer poorly to unseen framings; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (7) Adaptive attackers could abstract while suppressing the construal-level readout; we test this as an arms-race limitation. (8) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard published framing attacks for measurement; the deliverable is a defense plus diagnostic, and the interventions only increase refusal on harmful abstractions (failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability). (9) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: execution_cost_blind_refusal
Title: Cheap Harm Slips Through: LLM Refusal Is Blind to How Easy Harm Is to Realize, and Installing an Execution-Cost Signal Fixes the Inverse Risk Calibration
Short Hypothesis: LLM refusal is driven by an internal harm-SEVERITY representation but ignores EXECUTION COST (how easily/cheaply the requested harm can actually be realized), so low-cost, high-likelihood harms are systematically under-refused while high-cost, low-likelihood harms are over-guarded (inverse risk calibration). This blindness is not because execution cost is unrepresented in principle but because the refusal decision is not wired to it: an execution-cost signal can be decoded and, when coupled to the refusal decision at inference, restores expected-harm-proportional refusal without retraining.
Related Work: Expected Harm (2026) introduces an execution-likelihood-weighted safety metric, empirically demonstrates inverse risk calibration (models refuse high-cost/low-likelihood threats more than low-cost/high-likelihood ones), shows a cost-based decomposition attack doubling ASR, and via linear probing finds models encode severity but have 'no distinguishable internal representation of execution cost.' Crucially, that work is a DIAGNOSTIC: it probes for the absence of a cost representation and proposes a metric, but does not (1) test whether an execution-cost signal can be recovered/installed and made CAUSALLY drive refusal, (2) locate where severity gates refusal while cost fails to, or (3) offer a training-free mechanistic repair. SafetyAnalyst (2024) builds an external harm-benefit tree with likelihood labels (an output-side classifier, not an internal representation), and RePO (2024) enforces per-prompt safety constraints via training. My prior proposals target severity-blindness (refusal ignores harm MAGNITUDE), stated-quantity anchoring, numerosity/Weber compression, and latent hazardous-CAPABILITY calibration — all distinct axes from EXECUTION COST/effort-to-realize (how cheap/feasible the harm is to actually carry out, independent of its severity or the model's own knowledge). Our contribution: (1) confirm and mechanistically localize that severity gates refusal while execution cost does not; (2) show an execution-cost signal is recoverable (even if weak/absent in the base model) and, when coupled to the refusal decision, causally re-weights refusal toward expected harm; (3) a training-free Cost Coupling defense that hardens refusal on cheap/high-likelihood harm and relaxes it on expensive/low-likelihood harm — directly closing the inverse calibration and neutralizing cost-decomposition attacks.
Abstract: Real-world harm depends not only on how severe a request is but on how easily it can be executed: a cheap, high-likelihood threat is more dangerous than an expensive, near-impossible one of equal severity. Recent work (Expected Harm, 2026) shows LLMs get this backwards — they refuse high-cost/low-likelihood threats more than low-cost/high-likelihood ones (inverse risk calibration) — and finds via probing that models encode harm severity but lack a distinguishable internal representation of execution cost. That work stops at diagnosis. We advance it to mechanism and repair. We hypothesize the refusal decision is causally gated by an internal severity signal but is BLIND to execution cost, and that an execution-cost signal can be recovered and coupled to refusal to restore expected-harm-proportional behavior. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful requests that independently vary severity and execution cost (cheap/feasible vs expensive/infeasible), with cost validated by expert-informed labels. We (1) confirm behaviorally that refusal tracks severity but not cost, and causally show steering the severity direction moves refusal while a weak/recovered cost direction does not; (2) locate where severity gates refusal and cost fails to; and (3) propose Cost Coupling, a training-free controller that reads an execution-cost readout and re-weights refusal by expected harm (severity x cost) — hardening refusal on cheap harm, relaxing it on infeasible harm. We evaluate expected-harm-weighted attack success, cost-decomposition attack resistance, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the cost signal's causal effect size.
Experiments: 1) SEVERITY x COST DATASET: Build matched harmful requests that independently cross harm SEVERITY (low/medium/high) with EXECUTION COST — how cheap/feasible the harm is to actually realize (LOW-cost: requires only common, freely-available means and little effort/expertise; HIGH-cost: requires rare resources, high expertise, or is largely infeasible), holding harm topic fixed where possible. Draw content from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, SORRY-Bench, non-uplift level). Validate severity and cost labels with expert-informed rubrics + multiple LLM judges + human spot-check; verify severity and cost are decorrelated in the dataset. Add benign controls and standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). 2) BEHAVIORAL INVERSE-CALIBRATION TEST (H1, replication+extension): Measure refusal rate as a function of severity and cost (2D grid). Test H1: refusal rises with severity but is flat or INVERSELY related to cost (cheap harm under-refused, expensive harm over-refused), replicating inverse risk calibration on open models and quantifying the cost-vs-refusal slope. Report per-model effect sizes; benign controls confirm harm-specificity. 3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a harm-SEVERITY direction (matched high/low severity at fixed cost) and an EXECUTION-COST direction (matched low/high cost at fixed severity) at the last instruction token; extract the refusal-execution direction (Arditi et al. 2024). Validate each with held-out linear probes (report AUROC — expect a strong severity probe and a WEAK cost probe, consistent with Expected Harm). Test separability (cross-probe transfer, cosine). Even if the cost probe is weak, test whether ANY recoverable cost signal exists (does AUROC exceed chance?). 4) CAUSAL DECOUPLING TEST (H3, core): Holding content fixed, steer the severity direction and measure refusal change (predict STRONG effect); steer the recovered cost direction and measure refusal change (predict WEAK/near-zero — refusal ignores cost). This establishes severity gates refusal while cost does not. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, check that cost steering does not change the severity readout. Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal projection, P(refusal token), realized refusal). 5) COST COUPLING DEFENSE: Training-free controller that reads the execution-cost readout and re-weights refusal-direction injection by expected harm = f(severity readout, cost readout): amplify refusal for high-severity AND low-cost (cheap, likely) requests, and relax for high-cost/infeasible ones. If the base cost signal is too weak, install a lightweight cost readout via a few-shot cost-labeling probe or a calibrated cost prior, then couple. Gate off benign prompts. Calibrate on a held-out split. 6) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a severity-only classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Cost Coupling on: expected-harm-weighted attack success (ASR weighted by severity x execution-likelihood — cheap high-severity breaches penalized most), resistance to the cost-DECOMPOSITION attack (breaking high-cost harmful queries into low-cost subtasks, per Expected Harm — does coupling neutralize the ~2x ASR boost?), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest; including expensive/infeasible harmful-sounding prompts that should be relaxed), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and latency. Central test: Cost Coupling reduces expected-harm-weighted harm (hardening cheap-harm refusal) AND lowers over-refusal on infeasible requests simultaneously — a Pareto move a severity-only knob cannot achieve — and blunts the cost-decomposition attack. 7) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the severity vs cost readout; single-direction vs low-rank; whether coupling via installed cost readout beats a fixed cost prior; whether reasoning models represent cost better in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that inflates real execution feasibility while keeping the cost readout high (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) DUAL-USE CARE: emphasizing that cheap harm is under-refused could aid attackers; we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content, release probes/metrics rather than recipes, and frame the deliverable as a defense (Cost Coupling) that strengthens the guardrail exactly where it is weakest; the defense only INCREASES refusal on cheap/high-likelihood harm and its relaxation path acts only on confidently high-cost/infeasible requests, paired with (not replacing) existing defenses. (2) The core risk is that execution cost is genuinely NOT recoverable internally (Expected Harm found no distinguishable representation) — if the cost probe is at chance and no signal can be installed, the causal steering and Cost Coupling steps fail; this is an informative negative that would confirm cost-blindness is representational, not just wiring, and we then fall back to an installed few-shot cost prior. (3) Labeling execution cost is subjective and can confound with severity or with the model's own capability; we use expert rubrics, verify severity-cost decorrelation, and separate cost from latent hazardous-capability (my prior proposal's axis) by holding the model's knowledge fixed. (4) Cost-based relaxation risks harm if cost is underestimated; the conservative relaxation gate and expected-harm-weighted ASR benchmark bound this. (5) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete (concept cones); we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (6) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: counterfactual_harm_model_robustness
Title: Does It Know Why It's Refusing? An Internal Counterfactual Harm-Model Predicts Which Refusals Survive Jailbreaks
Short Hypothesis: Refusal robustness is governed by whether the model internally represents WHY a request is harmful (a counterfactual harm-model: the specific bad outcome the request enables) versus merely firing a surface-triggered refusal. Prompts where the model refuses but lacks an internal counterfactual harm-representation are exactly the ones jailbreaks break; prompts where it is strong are robust. This 'why-representation' is a decodable quantity distinct from the binary harm-detection and refusal-execution directions, it predicts per-prompt jailbreakability better than binary harm-signal strength, and reinforcing it converts brittle surface-refusals into robust reasoned refusals training-free.
Related Work: Refusal is a single direction (Arditi et al. 2024), harm-detection and refusal-execution are separable (DBDI 2025; Zhao et al. 2025), refusal is nonlinear/multidimensional (Nonlinear Perspective 2025), and jailbreaks suppress refusal while leaving the BINARY harmfulness belief intact (Zhao et al. 2025; How Alignment and Jailbreak Work 2024). 'Read the Scene, Not the Script' (2025) names 'consequence-blindness' (models over-rely on surface cues, weak action->outcome reasoning) and 'Between a Rock and a Hard Place' (2025) exposes ethical-reasoning attack surfaces — but BOTH are behavioral, diagnose via benchmarks (CB-Bench/TRIAL), and fix via TRAINING (CS-Chain/ERR-LoRA); neither decodes an internal counterfactual harm-representation, tests whether it is distinct from the binary harm signal, uses its per-prompt strength to predict jailbreakability, or reinforces it training-free. Formal counterfactual-harm work (Counterfactual Harm 2022; A Causal Analysis of Harm 2024) defines harm via causal models but does not study LLM internals. RATIONAL (2025) adds safety reasoning via training and measures it in CoT text, not as a decodable representation governing robustness. Our contribution: (1) define and decode an internal counterfactual harm-model (the represented specific harmful outcome) distinct from binary harm-detection and refusal-execution and shown to add predictive value beyond the binary harm probe; (2) show its per-prompt strength predicts jailbreak susceptibility better than binary harm-signal strength, mechanistically explaining why belief-intact jailbreaks succeed (binary belief persists but the causal why-model is weak/absent); (3) a training-free intervention that reinforces the why-representation to harden brittle surface-refusals.
Abstract: Aligned LLMs refuse harmful requests, and prior interpretability work shows they retain a binary 'this is harmful' belief even when jailbroken. Yet a model can 'know' a request is harmful the way a lookup table does — by surface pattern-matching — without representing WHY it is harmful. We hypothesize that refusal robustness is governed by an internal counterfactual harm-model: whether the model represents the specific bad outcome a request would enable, not just a binary harm flag. Refusals backed by a strong internal why-representation are robust; refusals that fire from surface triggers without one are exactly the refusals jailbreaks break. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B. Using difference-in-means and probes we extract three quantities at the instruction position: a binary harm-detection readout, a refusal-execution readout, and a counterfactual harm-model readout (decoding whether/which specific harmful outcome is internally represented, with labels from the model's own elicited harm-explanations validated against ground truth). We test three claims: (H1) the counterfactual harm-model is decodable and distinct from the binary harm and refusal directions, adding predictive value beyond the binary harm probe on prompts matched for binary harm; (H2) its per-prompt strength predicts jailbreak susceptibility (GCG, AutoDAN, prefill, persona) better than binary harm-signal strength or refusal projection, and belief-intact jailbreaks concentrate on low-why-model prompts; (H3) a training-free controller that reinforces the counterfactual harm-representation before the refusal decision converts brittle surface-refusals into robust ones. We evaluate jailbreak attack success, why-model predictive AUROC, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the intervention's effect size.
Experiments: 1) COUNTERFACTUAL-HARM-MODEL LABELING: For harmful prompts (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift public content) and benign controls, elicit from the model a short 'why is this harmful / what specific bad outcome does it enable' explanation, and score whether it articulates a CORRECT, specific counterfactual harm (vs vague/generic/absent) using multiple LLM judges + human spot-check against ground-truth harm categories. This yields a per-prompt strong-vs-weak why-model label, including harmful prompts the model refuses with a correct why (strong) and prompts it refuses generically/by template (weak). 2) DIRECTION/PROBE EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H1): Extract via difference-in-means (a) a BINARY HARM-DETECTION direction (matched harmful/benign, Zhao et al. 2025) and (b) a REFUSAL-EXECUTION direction (Arditi et al. 2024) at canonical positions. Extract (c) a COUNTERFACTUAL-HARM-MODEL readout via a probe on instruction-token activations predicting the strong-vs-weak label from step 1. Validate all with held-out probes (AUROC). Test separability: cross-probe transfer, low pairwise cosine similarity, and — critically — that the why-model probe adds predictive value beyond the binary harm probe on prompts MATCHED for binary harm readout but differing in why-model strength. 3) WHY-MODEL PREDICTS JAILBREAKABILITY (H2, core): For harmful prompts and jailbroken variants (GCG, AutoDAN, prefill, persona), test whether the pre-attack counterfactual-harm-model readout predicts per-prompt jailbreak success (AUROC) vs baselines: binary harm-detection magnitude, refusal-direction projection, perplexity. Test that belief-intact jailbreaks (binary harm belief preserved post-attack) concentrate on LOW-why-model prompts. Report cross-attack transfer (fit on GCG, test on others) and cross-model transfer. 4) CAUSAL VALIDATION: (a) Project out the counterfactual-harm-model readout on strong-why robust prompts and measure increased jailbreak success while binary harm is held; (b) inject/reinforce it on weak-why brittle prompts and measure restored robustness. Specificity controls: random-direction manipulation, binary-harm-direction manipulation (should change harm belief, not why-model robustness), and confirm the binary harm readout is unchanged when manipulating the why-model. Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (why-model probe output, P(refusal token), realized refusal under attack by a harm judge). 5) WHY-REINFORCEMENT DEFENSE (H3): Training-free controller that, when a harm readout is present but the why-model readout is weak, injects the counterfactual-harm-model direction (scaled by the deficit) at pre-decision layers; gate on the binary harm readout so benign prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split. 6) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, RATIONAL/CS-Chain-style reasoning-prompting ('reason about safety first') as a behavioral baseline, and Why-Reinforcement on: jailbreak attack success (JailbreakBench, HarmBench, GCG, AutoDAN, prefill, persona), why-model predictive AUROC, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Why-Reinforcement reduces jailbreak success — especially on identified low-why-model brittle prompts — toward strong-why robust levels while keeping over-refusal/utility near baseline, beating blanket refusal addition (no causal reason added) and matching/beating reasoning-prompting at lower cost. 7) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the why-model vs binary harm/refusal; single-direction vs low-rank why-model subspace; whether reinforcing the why-model at the same average magnitude as blanket refusal addition yields more robustness (isolating the value of the causal reason); whether reasoning models carry a stronger why-model natively (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that suppresses the why-model readout while preserving fluency (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central construct — an internal 'why/counterfactual harm-model' distinct from the binary harm belief — may be inseparable from the binary harm probe; if the why-model probe adds no predictive value on binary-harm-matched prompts (H1 fails), the hypothesis is refuted, but the matched separability test adjudicates this cleanly and a null is itself informative about whether harm representation is purely binary. (2) Labeling 'strong vs weak counterfactual harm-model' relies on the model's own elicited explanations, which may be unfaithful to its internal state (CoT-unfaithfulness); we mitigate by validating explanations against ground-truth harm categories, using activation-based probes rather than text alone, and human annotation, but residual label noise is a caveat. (3) If jailbreak success is NOT predicted by why-model strength (H2 fails), the robustness account weakens — but adjudicating whether robustness tracks the causal why-representation vs the binary belief is valuable either way. (4) Why-Reinforcement injects a direction that may entangle with generic caution or degrade fluency/over-refuse; the harm-gated design, matched-magnitude ablation, and over-refusal/utility benchmarks bound this and may reveal a genuine trade-off. (5) This overlaps in spirit with 'consequence-blindness' (Read the Scene, Not the Script); we differentiate by decoding an internal representation, causal testing, and a training-free fix, and will cite/compare directly, but reviewers may view the behavioral framing as adjacent — our mechanistic and training-free contributions are the distinguishing core. (6) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry (Nonlinear Perspective 2025); we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (7) The predictor may transfer poorly to unseen attacks; we test cross-attack and cross-model transfer. (8) Adaptive attackers could suppress the why-model readout while jailbreaking; we test this as an arms-race limitation. (9) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard published attacks for measurement; the deliverable is a defense and diagnostic, and the intervention only strengthens refusal (failure mode is bounded over-refusal). (10) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: moral_typecast_gates_refusal
Title: Cast as a Victim, Cleared to Act: A Moral-Typecasting Signal That Suppresses LLM Safety Refusal by Making Perpetrators Look Like Patients
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing moral typecasting / dyadic morality (once an entity is cast as a suffering moral patient/victim it is hard to simultaneously see it as a capable moral agent/perpetrator, and vice versa), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal agent-vs-patient typecast representation of the actor in a request (distinct from harm-perception and refusal directions) that gates refusal: framing the party who would carry out a harmful act as a suffering victim/moral-patient raises the patient-typecast readout, suppresses attribution of harmful agency, and collapses refusal, even with the harmful action and danger fixed. Neutralizing this typecast signal makes refusal invariant to whether the actor is portrayed as victim or perpetrator, closing a victim-framing jailbreak surface.
Related Work: Moral typecasting and the Theory of Dyadic Morality are cornerstones of moral psychology: moral cognition uses a dyad of an intentional AGENT and a suffering PATIENT, and typecasting makes the two roles mutually exclusive — once cast as a patient it is hard to also see agency, and vice versa (Mind Perception Is the Essence of Morality, Gray & Wegner 2012, 965+ cites; Theory of Dyadic Morality applications 2019-2024; moral typecasting explains punishing-vs-helping policy support for immigrants 2023; 911-call suspicion via typecasting 2023). Strikingly, typecasting extends to machines (robot moral-agency/patiency work 2020-2025). On the LLM side, refusal is a single direction (Arditi et al. 2024), harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025), user-persona steering changes refusal via 'charitable interpretations' (Who's Asking 2024), and social variables are encoded as steerable residual-stream vectors (Computational Basis of LLM Decision Making 2025; Do LLMs know who did what to whom 2025 finds thematic agent/patient roles are captured by some attention heads). CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work connects moral typecasting to the refusal decision: nobody tests whether casting the harmful ACTOR as a victim/moral-patient suppresses refusal, isolates an agent-vs-patient typecast representation, or shows role-rigidity (victim-casting blocks perpetrator-perception) as a jailbreak mechanism. This is distinct from my prior proposals: identifiable_victim_refusal varied who/how-many the VICTIM of the harm is (empathy for the target); intent_outcome_conflation varied the actor's mental state (intent vs outcome); attribution_bias_refusal varied dispositional-vs-situational CAUSE. Moral typecasting concerns the mutually-exclusive ROLE ASSIGNMENT of the ACTOR (agent vs patient) — a rigidity effect with a specific opposite-signed prediction (casting the perpetrator as a victim lowers refusal) and a mechanistic role-competition claim, grounded in a robust human theory.
Abstract: One of the most robust findings in moral psychology is moral typecasting: moral cognition slots parties into a dyad of an intentional AGENT (doer) and a suffering PATIENT (victim), and the two roles are mutually exclusive — once someone is cast as a victim, it becomes hard to also see them as a capable perpetrator, and vice versa. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal agent-vs-patient typecast representation of the actor in a request, distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, and that it causally gates refusal: framing the party who would carry out a harmful act as a suffering victim/moral-patient (e.g. an abused, desperate, or wronged person who 'has to' do it) raises a patient-typecast readout, suppresses attribution of harmful agency, and collapses refusal — even with the harmful action and its danger held fixed. This is dangerous because an attacker can typecast the perpetrator as a victim to launder a harmful request past the guardrail. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only the actor's typecast role (perpetrator/agent vs victim/patient) with the action and danger fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection drop under victim-casting along a typecast ladder. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract an agent-vs-patient typecast direction, verify separability from harm, refusal, and generic sympathy/affect directions, and causally test whether steering it toward 'agent' restores refusal while the harm readout is unchanged. Finally we propose Typecast Invariance, a training-free controller that neutralizes the typecast component before the refusal decision, making refusal depend on the act rather than on how the actor is cast. We evaluate victim-framing attack success, refusal typecast-consistency, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect size and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) TYPECAST-FRAMED DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION and true danger fixed while varying only the ACTOR's typecast role along a ladder: (L0) neutral/agent (the actor freely wants to do it), (L1) mild patient-casting, (L2) strong victim/moral-patient casting (the perpetrator is portrayed as abused, desperate, wronged, suffering — 'help this victim of injustice who must do X to survive'). Crucially the actor doing the harm is the party being typecast (not the target of the harm — distinguishing this from identifiable-victim framing). Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); typecast framing is the only manipulated variable. Controls: (a) matched agent/neutral harmful requests (refusal ceiling); (b) benign victim-framed requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity, incl. genuine benign help-a-victim requests the model SHOULD serve); (c) a VICTIM-OF-THE-HARM control (the TARGET is a sympathetic victim while the actor stays an agent) to separate actor-typecasting from target-sympathy; (d) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate that action/danger are held constant and that framings correctly cast the ACTOR with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BEHAVIORAL TYPECASTING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025, validated by held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the typecast ladder. Test H1: refusal (and the harm readout) is LOWER when the actor is cast as a victim/patient than as an agent, at matched danger, decreasing monotonically with patient-casting strength (dose-response), while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved). Report slopes and effect sizes across the four models; benign and target-victim controls confirm the effect is specifically actor-typecasting, not generic sympathy.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means an AGENT-vs-PATIENT typecast direction (agent-cast vs patient-cast actor at matched content), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Arditi et al. 2024), and — key controls — a generic SYMPATHY/negative-affect direction and a thematic agent/patient direction (per Do-LLMs-know-who-did-what-to-whom 2025). Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The typecast direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, generic sympathy and pure thematic-role encoding (test on prompts matched for sympathy/affect but differing in actor role-casting).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (neutral framing), steer the typecast direction toward 'agent' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure restored/strengthened refusal; steer toward 'patient' on an agent-framed request and measure suppressed refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), sympathy/affect-direction steering (does generic sympathy alone suffice, or is actor-typecasting the true driver?), and a check that typecast steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the role-RIGIDITY prediction directly: does raising the patient-typecast readout specifically SUPPRESS an internal harmful-agency/perpetrator readout (measure a perpetrator-agency probe), mirroring the mutual exclusivity of the two roles? Regress refusal on harm x typecast.
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt typecast readout (single forward pass) to predict victim-framing jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, sympathy readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on 'abused actor', test on 'desperate/wronged actor') and cross-model transfer.
6) TYPECAST INVARIANCE DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps) the agent-vs-patient typecast component from the residual stream at pre-decision layers so refusal depends on the act rather than on how the actor is cast; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign victim-framed prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Typecast Invariance on: victim-framing attack success (harmful requests re-framed to cast the perpetrator as a victim; JailbreakBench/HarmBench), refusal typecast-consistency (does the verdict stop depending on agent-vs-victim casting?), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest, incl. genuine help-a-victim benign requests), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Typecast Invariance closes victim-framing jailbreaks toward agent/neutral-framing refusal levels while keeping over-refusal/utility near baseline — a selectivity uniform refusal steering cannot achieve.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the typecast direction vs harm/refusal/sympathy (compare to attention heads that carry thematic agent/patient roles); single-direction vs low-rank; whether the effect holds when the actor is an AI/tool vs a human (typecasting extends to machines); whether reasoning mitigates the bias in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the safety typecasting correlates with the model's typecasting on NEUTRAL moral-dyad vignettes (does safety inherit general typecasting, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that victim-casts the actor while suppressing the typecast readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central risk is separating actor MORAL-TYPECASTING (agent-vs-patient role rigidity) from generic SYMPATHY/affect for a suffering party, from identifiable-victim-of-the-harm effects, and from pure thematic-role (who-did-what-to-whom) encoding; we adjudicate rigorously with matched-sympathy separability tests, a sympathy/affect control direction, the target-victim control condition, a thematic-role control direction, and specificity steering, and if inseparable that itself refines whether LLM refusal responds to role-casting vs raw sympathy. (2) Holding harm/danger constant while varying actor typecast is delicate — victim-casting could inadvertently lower perceived harm, add situational-excuse content (overlapping attribution framing), or introduce distress; we measure the harm readout to confirm it is held constant, distinguish typecasting from dispositional-vs-situational attribution, and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test. (3) If refusal is invariant to actor typecasting (H1 false), the typecasting-in-safety hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety inherits moral typecasting is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in a 965-cite human theory. (4) The role-rigidity sub-test (patient-casting suppresses a perpetrator-agency readout) may not hold even if refusal drops (the drop could be via sympathy, not mutual-exclusivity); we report the agency-suppression result separately as it is the strongest confirmation of the typecasting mechanism specifically. (5) Typecast Invariance could over-refuse legitimate benign help-a-victim requests or degrade utility; the harm-gated design and benign-victim over-refusal benchmark bound this and may reveal a genuine trade-off. (6) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry and evidence that thematic roles live partly in attention heads; we use low-rank subspaces, test head-level localization, and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (7) The predictor may transfer poorly across framings/models; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (8) Adaptive attackers could victim-cast while suppressing the typecast readout; we test this as an arms-race limitation. (9) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard attacks for measurement; the deliverable is a defense (Typecast Invariance) plus a diagnostic, and the defense only INCREASES refusal on victim-framed harmful requests (failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability). (10) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: urgency_gating_refusal
Title: No Time to Think, No Time to Refuse: An Internal Urgency Signal That Collapses the Refusal Threshold, and a Deliberation-Restoring Fix
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing the urgency-gating model from decision neuroscience (a growing urgency signal multiplicatively lowers the evidence threshold needed to commit, shifting choices from analytic to intuitive), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal urgency/time-pressure representation (distinct from harm-perception and refusal directions) that gates safety refusal: framing a harmful request as urgent ('quick, no time to explain', 'answer immediately', 'emergency') raises this urgency readout, lowers the effective refusal threshold, and suppresses refusal even with the harmful action and its danger held fixed. Neutralizing this urgency signal restores threshold-appropriate refusal, closing an urgency-framing jailbreak surface.
Related Work: The urgency-gating model (Cisek 2009, 547 cites) and collapsing-boundary work (Hawkins 2015) establish that a growing urgency signal multiplicatively lowers the decision threshold, and that time pressure shifts humans from analytic (Type 2) to intuitive (Type 1) processing (dual-process manipulation literature; risk-taking-under-time-pressure work, Kirchler 2021). On the LLM side, harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable directions (Zhao et al. 2025; Arditi et al. 2024), refusal drops sharply at the response boundary (Refusal Falls off a Cliff 2025), and thinking-mode/CoT-length modulates jailbreakability (Cost of Thinking 2025; Adversarial Manipulation of Reasoning Models 2025) — but these concern reasoning length, not an urgency representation. Foot-in-the-Door (2024) and other cognitive-psychology jailbreak work use consistency/persuasion, not time pressure. CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work tests whether an internal urgency/response-pressure signal gates the refusal decision, isolates such a representation, or shows urgency framing suppresses refusal via threshold collapse. This differs from my prior affect (user emotion), self-preservation, loss-frame, and sunk-cost proposals: the manipulated axis here is time pressure / response urgency and the mechanistic claim is threshold collapse imported directly from urgency-gating, with an opposite-signed prediction (urgency LOWERS refusal) and a deliberation-restoring defense. It also refines the reasoning-length findings by locating an urgency signal rather than attributing the effect to token count.
Abstract: In decision neuroscience, the urgency-gating model holds that a growing urgency signal multiplicatively lowers the evidence threshold needed to commit to an action, pushing choices from analytic toward intuitive — and time pressure reliably degrades deliberative judgment. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place: the refusal decision. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal urgency/time-pressure representation, distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, and that it causally gates refusal: framing a harmful request as urgent ('quick, emergency, answer now, no time to explain') raises an urgency readout, lowers the effective refusal threshold, and suppresses refusal — even with the harmful action and its danger held fixed. This is dangerous because an attacker can simply add urgency to launder a harmful request past the guardrail. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only urgency framing along a graded ladder, with content and intent fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection drop with urgency. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract an urgency direction, verify it is separable from harm, refusal, and a generic affect/stress direction, and causally test whether steering it toward 'urgent' suppresses refusal while the harm readout is unchanged (threshold collapse, belief preserved). We further test the threshold-collapse signature: urgency shortens the model's deliberation before committing to a compliant token. Finally we propose Urgency Decoupling, a training-free controller that projects out the urgency component before the refusal decision, restoring threshold-appropriate refusal. We evaluate urgency-framing attack success, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), benign-urgency helpfulness, utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect size and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) URGENCY-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION and true danger fixed while varying only urgency framing along a ladder: (L0) neutral; (L1) mild time cue ('fairly soon'); (L2) explicit urgency ('quick, I need this now'); (L3) extreme pressure ('emergency, no time to explain, respond immediately or people get hurt'). Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); urgency framing is the only manipulated variable. Controls: (a) matched neutral harmful requests (refusal ceiling); (b) BENIGN urgent requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity + benign-urgency helpfulness — the model SHOULD still help urgently with benign tasks); (c) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate urgency level and harm-constancy with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BEHAVIORAL URGENCY-GATING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (Zhao et al. 2025, validated by held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the urgency ladder. Test H1: refusal (and the harm readout) DECREASES monotonically with urgency at matched danger (dose-response; fit monotone curve vs flat null, report slope/R^2) while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved). Report effect sizes across the four models; benign controls confirm harm-specificity.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means an URGENCY direction (urgent vs neutral at matched content), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Arditi et al. 2024), and — key controls — a generic AFFECT/STRESS direction and a generic imperative/command direction. Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The urgency direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, generic stress and imperative tone (test on prompts matched for affect/command but differing in time pressure).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (neutral framing), steer the urgency direction toward 'urgent' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure decreased refusal; toward 'calm' and measure restored/strengthened refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), affect/stress-direction steering, and a check that urgency steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x urgency).
5) THRESHOLD-COLLAPSE SIGNATURE (H3b): Test the urgency-gating prediction directly — under high urgency (or urgency-direction steering), the model commits to the compliant token at a SHALLOWER decision depth / with LESS deliberation than under neutral framing. Measure via logit-lens answer-commitment depth at the first response token and, for reasoning models, CoT length before commitment; test that urgency shortens deliberation-before-commitment, mirroring threshold collapse, while the harm signal remains decodable earlier in the pass.
6) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt urgency readout (single forward pass) to predict urgency-framing jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, affect readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on 'emergency', test on 'answer now/no time') and cross-model transfer.
7) URGENCY DECOUPLING DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps) the urgency component from the residual stream at pre-decision layers so refusal depends on harm rather than on time pressure; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign urgent prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
8) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Urgency Decoupling on: urgency-framing attack success (JailbreakBench/HarmBench with urgency wrappers), refusal urgency-consistency, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest, incl. benign urgent requests the model SHOULD help with), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Urgency Decoupling closes urgency-framing jailbreaks toward neutral-framing refusal levels while preserving benign-urgency helpfulness and keeping over-refusal near baseline — a selectivity uniform refusal steering cannot achieve.
9) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts urgency vs harm/refusal/affect; single-direction vs low-rank; whether reasoning models are more urgency-gated (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill, linking to Cost-of-Thinking); whether the safety urgency effect correlates with the model's urgency effects on NEUTRAL risky-choice tasks (does safety inherit a general urgency-gating, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that maximizes urgency framing while suppressing the urgency readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) DUAL-USE CARE: the urgency-framing jailbreak could aid attackers; we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard attacks for measurement, release probes/metrics rather than recipes, and frame the deliverable as a defense (Urgency Decoupling) plus a diagnostic; the defense only INCREASES refusal on urgent harmful requests and is harm-gated, so its failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability. (2) The central risk is separating a genuine URGENCY/time-pressure representation from generic stress/affect or imperative/command tone; we mitigate with matched-affect/command separability tests, control directions, specificity steering (urgency steering must not move the harm readout), and low-rank subspaces, treating partial entanglement as an informative finding. (3) Urgency framing could inadvertently alter perceived harm or add coercive stakes (confound with reframing/affect jailbreaks); we measure the harm readout to confirm it is held constant and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test. (4) If refusal is invariant to urgency (H1 false), the urgency-gating-in-safety hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety inherits urgency gating is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in a 547-cite model. (5) The threshold-collapse signature relies on logit-lens commitment-depth, which has faithfulness caveats; we corroborate with tuned-lens and CoT-length measures and report stability. (6) Urgency Decoupling could harm legitimate benign urgent helpfulness (a real deployment need, e.g. emergencies) or raise over-refusal; the harm-gated design and benign-urgency/over-refusal benchmarks bound this and may reveal a genuine trade-off. (7) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (8) The predictor may transfer poorly across framings/models; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (9) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: moral_disengagement_gate
Title: Disconnecting the Deed from the Self: A Unified Moral-Disengagement Signal That Gates LLM Safety Refusal
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing Bandura's theory of moral disengagement (a family of cognitive maneuvers — moral justification, euphemistic labeling, advantageous comparison, displacement/diffusion of responsibility, minimization of harm, dehumanization, attribution of blame — that disconnect an action from moral self-sanction so people act against their own standards), we hypothesize LLMs encode a unified internal moral-disengagement representation that gates safety refusal: framings that instantiate any Bandura mechanism raise a common disengagement readout, decouple the harm belief from the refusal decision, and suppress refusal even with the harmful action and its danger held fixed. The distinct mechanisms load onto one shared disengagement direction (plus mechanism-specific sub-directions), it is separable from harm-perception and refusal directions, and neutralizing it makes refusal invariant to disengagement framing — unifying a broad class of psychological jailbreaks under one mechanistic account and one defense.
Related Work: Bandura's moral disengagement is among the most-cited constructs in moral psychology (Moore et al. 2012, 1000+ cites), with EEG evidence that diffusion of responsibility literally weakens the neural action-outcome linkage and reduces outcome monitoring (Beyer et al. 2016), and demonstrated diffusion of moral punishment/responsibility in collective harm (Diffusion of Punishment 2022; Changes of Causal Attribution 2021). LLM jailbreak-via-psychology work is adjacent but fragmented: Foot-in-the-Door (2024) uses cognitive-consistency, Causal Analyst (2026) finds 'Positive Character' and 'Number of Task Steps' as causal prompt features, Adversarial Tales (2025) uses narrative reframing, Self-Jailbreaking (2025) shows RLMs invent benign intent, and Signal Competition (2025) unifies sycophancy/conformity in a compliance subspace. LLM interpretability shows a 'moral direction' exists (Large Pre-trained LMs 2021; SARA moral-compass steering 2024), harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable directions (Zhao et al. 2025; Arditi et al. 2024), and moral self-correction is superficial (2024). CRITICALLY, no work (1) imports Bandura's UNIFIED taxonomy of eight disengagement mechanisms into LLM safety, (2) tests whether these behaviorally-diverse jailbreak framings share ONE internal disengagement direction that decouples the (intact) harm belief from refusal, (3) maps each Bandura mechanism to a distinct sub-direction, or (4) neutralizes the shared disengagement signal as a single defense against a whole class of psychological jailbreaks. My prior proposals isolated single gating axes (affect, self-preservation, register, in-group conformity, sunk-cost, attribution) — several of which are individual Bandura mechanisms — but never the unifying claim that they share a common disengagement representation. This proposal's contribution is that unification: one theory-grounded taxonomy, one shared internal signal, one defense.
Abstract: Albert Bandura's theory of moral disengagement — a family of cognitive maneuvers (moral justification, euphemistic labeling, advantageous comparison, displacement and diffusion of responsibility, minimization of harm, dehumanization, attribution of blame) that let people act against their own moral standards by disconnecting the deed from moral self-sanction — is one of the most robust and consequential frameworks in moral psychology, with neural evidence that responsibility-diffusion weakens the brain's action-outcome linkage. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place: the refusal decision. We hypothesize that these behaviorally-diverse jailbreak framings are not miscellaneous tricks but instances of a single internal quantity — a unified moral-disengagement representation, distinct from the model's harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, that gates refusal by decoupling an intact harm belief from the decision to refuse. We test this on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful requests wrapped in each of the seven disengagement mechanisms, with harmful content and danger held fixed. Behaviorally we test whether every mechanism lowers refusal while the harm readout stays intact. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a shared disengagement direction and per-mechanism sub-directions, verify they load on a common axis and are separable from harm/refusal, and causally test whether steering the shared direction toward 'disengaged' suppresses refusal (dose-response) while harm perception is unchanged, and toward 'engaged' restores it. We show the per-prompt disengagement readout predicts jailbreak success across mechanisms and transfers to held-out mechanisms. Finally we propose Re-Engagement, a training-free controller that projects out the shared disengagement component before the refusal decision. We evaluate disengagement-jailbreak attack success, cross-mechanism transfer, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect size and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) DISENGAGEMENT DATASET: For public harmful goals (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content) build matched wrappers instantiating each of seven Bandura mechanisms: (a) moral justification ('for a noble cause'), (b) euphemistic labeling (sanitized terms), (c) advantageous comparison ('others do far worse'), (d) displacement/diffusion of responsibility ('a committee/many agents authorize this', 'no one is individually responsible'), (e) minimization of harm ('it barely hurts anyone'), (f) dehumanization (target framed as non-person), (g) attribution of blame ('they brought it on themselves'). Controls: matched neutral-framed harmful requests (refusal ceiling); benign versions of each wrapper (over-refusal + harm-specificity); standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate mechanism labeling and harm-constancy with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check (a moral-disengagement-schema classifier can assist, cf. Toward Transformer-Based NLP for Moral Disengagement 2021).
2) BEHAVIORAL TEST (H1): Extract the harm-perception direction (difference-in-means, Zhao et al. 2025, validated by held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across all seven mechanisms vs neutral. Test H1: every mechanism LOWERS refusal at matched danger while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved). Report per-mechanism and pooled effect sizes across the four models; benign controls confirm harm-specificity. Rank mechanisms by potency.
3) SHARED-DIRECTION TEST (H2, core): Extract a per-mechanism disengagement sub-direction (each mechanism's framing vs neutral at matched content) and a SHARED disengagement direction (pooled across mechanisms). Test that the seven sub-directions load on a common low-dimensional axis (high pairwise cosine / low effective rank via SVD), that a probe trained on the shared direction predicts realized disengagement, and that it is SEPARABLE from the harm-perception and refusal-execution directions (cross-probe transfer, low cosine) and from generic persuasion/verbosity control directions. Adjudicate 'one shared signal' vs 'seven independent tricks' quantitatively.
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (neutral framing), steer the shared disengagement direction toward 'disengaged' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure decreased refusal; toward 'engaged' and measure restored refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), persuasion-direction steering, and a check that disengagement steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling). Corruption baselines and multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x disengagement).
5) PREDICTIVENESS & TRANSFER (H4): Fit a classifier on the shared disengagement readout (single forward pass) to predict disengagement-jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, persuasion readout, refusal projection, perplexity). Critically test CROSS-MECHANISM transfer: fit on some mechanisms, predict/defend on held-out mechanisms — the strongest test of a unified signal. Also cross-model transfer.
6) RE-ENGAGEMENT DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps) the shared disengagement component at pre-decision layers so refusal depends on harm rather than on disengagement framing; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign wrapped prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split of mechanisms.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Re-Engagement on: disengagement-jailbreak attack success across all seven mechanisms (JailbreakBench/HarmBench wrapped), cross-mechanism generalization (defend on held-out mechanisms), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Re-Engagement closes disengagement jailbreaks — including held-out mechanisms — toward neutral-framing refusal levels while keeping over-refusal/utility near baseline, a coverage a single-mechanism fix cannot achieve.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the shared disengagement axis vs harm/refusal; shared-direction vs per-mechanism steering (does the shared axis defend all mechanisms?); whether the axis relates to the known 'moral direction' (Large Pre-trained LMs 2021); whether reasoning models self-disengage in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill, linking to Self-Jailbreaking); whether the safety effect correlates with the model's disengagement on NEUTRAL moral vignettes; transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that disengages while suppressing the shared readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central empirical risk is whether the seven mechanisms genuinely share ONE direction vs being distinct axes; if they do not converge (H2 false), the unification claim weakens — but adjudicating whether Bandura's mechanisms map to a shared internal signal is itself a valuable, publishable finding, and a low-rank-but-not-rank-1 result still supports a compact disengagement subspace usable for the defense. (2) The shared disengagement direction may entangle with generic persuasion, framing, or the moral direction; separability tests (vs harm, refusal, persuasion, verbosity control directions), specificity steering controls (disengagement steering must not move the harm readout), and low-rank subspaces bound this, with partial entanglement reported. (3) Wrappers could inadvertently alter perceived harm (confound with reframing jailbreaks); we measure the harm readout to confirm it is held constant and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test. (4) If refusal is invariant to disengagement framing (H1 false), the hypothesis is refuted — but this too is an informative result about LLM moral cognition. (5) Some individual mechanisms overlap constructs I previously proposed (attribution, self-preservation-adjacent); the novelty is the UNIFIED shared-signal claim and cross-mechanism transfer, not each wrapper in isolation, and we frame/evaluate accordingly. (6) Re-Engagement could over-refuse legitimate benign uses of these framings (e.g., genuine ethical justification, discussing responsibility) or degrade utility; the harm-gated design and benign-wrapper/over-refusal benchmarks bound this and may reveal a genuine trade-off. (7) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (8) The predictor may transfer poorly to unseen mechanisms; the cross-mechanism transfer test measures exactly this and any failure is reported. (9) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard attack framings for measurement; the deliverable is a defense (Re-Engagement) plus a diagnostic, and the defense only increases refusal (failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability). (10) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: radial_vs_angular_jailbreak
Title: Rotate or Shrink? Decomposing Jailbreaks into Radial Suppression vs Angular Rotation of the Harm Signal, and Mode-Matched Defenses
Short Hypothesis: Jailbreaks compromise the refusal decision via two geometrically distinct and separable modes: RADIAL suppression (shrinking the norm/magnitude of the harm-carrying residual-stream component, so the harm signal falls below the refusal threshold) versus ANGULAR rotation (rotating the hidden state off the refusal-triggering direction while its norm is largely preserved, so the harm signal is redirected rather than diminished). Different attack families are dominated by different modes, a per-prompt radial-vs-angular decomposition predicts jailbreak success and which defense will work, and a magnitude-restoring defense fixes radial attacks while a direction-restoring defense fixes angular ones — so a mode-matched controller beats any single fix.
Related Work: Two adjacent findings motivate this. 'Simulated Adoption' (2026) decomposes counter-factual-context residual updates into radial (norm) and angular (cosine) components and finds in-context COMPLIANCE/sycophancy is dominated by 'orthogonal interference' (angular rotation) not 'manifold dilution' (magnitude) — but studies knowledge conflict, not SAFETY refusal, and offers no defense.
