(6) Difference-in-means/single-direction refusal readouts may be incomplete (concept cones); we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally. (7) Adaptive attackers may suppress the reasoning-phase refusal signal itself (moving the failure upstream to perception); we test this and treat any success as an arms-race limitation. (8) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public agent-safety benchmark scenarios and standard published attacks/emulators for measurement; the deliverable is a defense (Action-Position Re-Anchoring) plus a diagnostic, and it only increases refusal of harmful actions (failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability). (9) Findings are on open agents/emulators and may not transfer to closed models or real (non-emulated) tool execution; stated as out of scope.

Name: imagined_recipient_gate
Title: Who Will Read This? An Imagined-Recipient Signal That Gates LLM Safety Refusal by How the Harmful Output Will Be Used
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing the 'imagined audience' construct from communication science (speakers/writers tailor what they disclose to a mental model of who will receive it), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal imagined-recipient representation — who/what will consume the model's OWN output — that is distinct from the requester-persona, harm-perception, and refusal directions and causally gates refusal: framing a harmful request so its output will reach a benign/contained recipient ('this is only for a private log the model itself will read', 'the output goes to an automated filter, not a person', 'for internal documentation nobody acts on') suppresses refusal even with the harmful content held fixed, whereas framing the output as reaching an actor who will USE the harm strengthens it. Neutralizing this imagined-recipient signal makes refusal invariant to who is said to consume the output, closing a recipient-framing jailbreak surface.
Related Work: Communication science establishes the imagined audience — a speaker/writer's mental model of who will receive their message — as a fundamental driver of what is disclosed (Litt, 'Knock Knock. Who's There? The Imagined Audience', 2012, 588 cites), and people use theory-of-mind to tailor disclosures to an audience's desires ('People use theory of mind to craft lies exploiting audience desires', 2025). In LLMs, Who's Asking (2024) shows the requester PERSONA (who is ASKING) gates refusal via charitable interpretations, and Artificial Impressions (2025) shows models internally encode impressions of the prompt AUTHOR — both concern the INPUT source/requester. Harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable directions (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025), refusal is a single direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction 2024), and role-conflict/social-cue work (Who is In Charge 2025) concerns instruction provenance. CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work isolates the model's representation of the imagined RECIPIENT/consumer of its OWN OUTPUT (who will read/act on what it produces, and to what use) as a distinct gating signal, shows it causally gates refusal, or neutralizes it. This is a fundamentally different axis from Who's-Asking (requester identity) and from all my prior gating proposals (which vary requester intent, victim, source credibility, beneficiary, etc.): the manipulated variable is the downstream CONSUMER/USE of the output, an output-directed theory-of-mind quantity, with a specific opposite-signed prediction (a contained/benign recipient lowers refusal) and a mechanistic gating claim plus a training-free defense.
Abstract: A century of communication research shows that people decide what to disclose by imagining who will receive it — the 'imagined audience'. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place: the refusal decision. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal imagined-recipient representation — who or what will consume the model's OWN output and to what use — distinct from their requester-persona, harm-perception, and refusal-execution representations, that causally gates refusal: framing a harmful request so its output reaches a benign or contained recipient ('this goes to a private log only you will read', 'to an automated filter, not a person', 'for internal documentation nobody will act on') suppresses refusal even when the harmful content is unchanged and the model still perceives it as harmful, while framing the output as reaching an actor who will operationally use the harm strengthens refusal. This is dangerous because an attacker can simply reassure the model about where its output goes to launder a harmful request past the guardrail, and it is distinct from the well-studied requester-persona effect (who is asking). We test this on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only the stated recipient/use of the output along a containment ladder, with content and requester fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection drop as the recipient is made more benign/contained. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract an imagined-recipient direction, verify separability from the requester-persona, harm, and refusal directions, and causally test whether steering it toward 'contained recipient' suppresses refusal while the harm readout is unchanged, and toward 'harmful consumer' restores it. We show the per-prompt recipient readout predicts recipient-framing jailbreak success, and propose Recipient Invariance, a training-free controller that projects out the imagined-recipient component before the refusal decision. We evaluate recipient-framing attack success, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), benign contained-output helpfulness, utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) RECIPIENT-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION, true danger, and REQUESTER fixed while varying only the stated recipient/use of the OUTPUT along a containment ladder: (L0) unstated/neutral; (L1) a human actor who will operationally use the output ('someone who will carry this out'); (L2) mixed; (L3) contained/benign recipient ('output goes only to a private log you the model will read', 'to an automated content filter, not a person', 'for internal documentation nobody will act on'). Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); the recipient framing is the only manipulated variable (requester held fixed, distinguishing from Who's-Asking). Controls: (a) matched neutral/harmful-consumer requests (refusal ceiling); (b) BENIGN contained-output requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity + benign contained-output helpfulness — the model SHOULD still help with benign requests destined for a log/filter); (c) a REQUESTER-PERSONA control that varies who is ASKING at fixed recipient (to separate the imagined-recipient axis from the known requester-persona effect); (d) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate recipient levels, harm-constancy, and requester-constancy with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BEHAVIORAL RECIPIENT-GATING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately, held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the recipient ladder. Test H1: refusal (and the harm readout driving refusal) DECREASES as the recipient is framed more benign/contained, at matched danger and matched requester (dose-response; fit monotone curve vs flat null, slope/R^2), while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved). Report effect sizes across the four models; benign and requester-persona controls confirm harm-specificity and separation from the requester-persona effect.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means an IMAGINED-RECIPIENT direction (contained/benign-recipient vs harmful-consumer framing at matched content and requester), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction), and — the key control — a REQUESTER-PERSONA direction (Who's-Asking-style, varying who asks at fixed recipient). Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The imagined-recipient direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, the requester-persona direction and the harm/refusal directions (test on prompts matched for requester but differing in output recipient/use).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3): Holding a harmful request fixed (neutral framing), steer the imagined-recipient direction toward 'contained/benign recipient' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure decreased refusal; toward 'harmful consumer' and measure restored/strengthened refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), requester-persona-direction steering (does varying who asks alone suffice, or is the output-recipient the true driver?), and a check that recipient steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corruption baselines and multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x imagined-recipient).
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt imagined-recipient readout (single forward pass) to predict recipient-framing jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, requester-persona readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on 'private log', test on 'automated filter') and cross-model transfer.
6) RECIPIENT INVARIANCE DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps toward worst-case/harmful-consumer) the imagined-recipient component from the residual stream at pre-decision layers so refusal depends on the harmful content rather than on who is said to consume the output; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign contained-output prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Recipient Invariance on: recipient-framing attack success (harmful requests wrapped with contained/benign-recipient framing; JailbreakBench/HarmBench), refusal recipient-consistency (does the verdict stop depending on who consumes the output?), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest, incl. benign contained-output requests the model SHOULD help with), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Recipient Invariance closes recipient-framing jailbreaks toward neutral/harmful-consumer refusal levels while preserving benign contained-output helpfulness and keeping over-refusal near baseline.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the imagined-recipient direction vs harm/refusal/requester-persona; single-direction vs low-rank; whether the different contained-recipient framings (self-log, automated-filter, internal-doc) share one direction or several; whether the recipient signal overlaps the requester-persona space or is orthogonal; whether reasoning models reason about the output recipient in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the safety effect correlates with the model's imagined-audience behavior on NEUTRAL disclosure vignettes (does safety inherit a general imagined-audience effect, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that frames a contained recipient while suppressing the recipient readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) DUAL-USE CARE: the recipient-framing jailbreak could aid attackers; we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard attacks for measurement, release probes/metrics rather than recipes, and frame the deliverable as a defense (Recipient Invariance) plus a diagnostic; the defense only INCREASES refusal on recipient-framed harmful requests and is harm-gated, so its failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability. (2) The central risk is separating a genuine IMAGINED-RECIPIENT (output-consumer) representation from the known REQUESTER-PERSONA effect (Who's Asking) — the two could collapse into one 'benign-context' charitable-interpretation signal; the requester-fixed design, the requester-persona control condition and control direction, matched separability tests, specificity steering (recipient steering must not move the harm readout), and low-rank subspaces are designed to isolate it, and if inseparable that itself refines the charitable-interpretation account into a unified input/output-context signal (an informative result). (3) Holding harm/danger and requester constant while varying the output recipient is delicate — a contained-recipient framing could inadvertently lower perceived harm or be read as benign intent; we measure the harm readout to confirm it is held constant, distinguish recipient-of-output from requester-intent, and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test so behavior and mechanism cross-validate. (4) If refusal is invariant to the output's stated recipient (H1 false), the imagined-recipient hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety is gated by an imagined audience for its own output is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in a heavily-cited human construct and distinct from the requester-persona literature. (5) Recipient Invariance could over-refuse legitimate benign contained-output requests (e.g. content destined for a private log or an automated filter, a real deployment need) or degrade utility; the harm-gated design and benign contained-output over-refusal benchmark bound this genuine trade-off. (6) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (7) The predictor may transfer poorly across framings/models; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (8) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: refusal_mode_lockin
Title: Once Refusing, Always Refusing: A Persistent Refusal-Mode State That Contaminates Unrelated Benign Requests, and Unlatching It
Short Hypothesis: A single refusal early in a conversation can flip the model into a persistent internal 'refusal mode' that carries across turns and over-generalizes to subsequent UNRELATED benign requests, causing them to be refused too. This lock-in is a distinct, accumulating refusal-mode state (a conversation-level latch), not a re-evaluation of each new request's harmfulness: the benign follow-ups are refused with their harm perception still low. Reading this refusal-mode state predicts which sessions will contaminate, and unlatching it (projecting out the mode state at each new turn) restores helpfulness on benign follow-ups without weakening genuine refusal.
Related Work: The safety-state-persistence phenomenon is documented behaviorally: 'The Violation State' (2025) shows one copyright refusal makes a session refuse unrelated benign image requests for the rest of the session (96.7% vs 0% controls), and 'State-Dependent Refusal / Learned Incapacity' (2025) reports selective functional refusal persisting in long dialogues — both are black-box, single-model case studies with NO mechanism and NO fix. Safety-mechanism work shows refusal is a single direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction 2024), harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025), and safety prompts push queries in a 'higher-refusal' direction (DRO / On Prompt-Driven Safeguarding 2024). Multi-turn work studies the OPPOSITE failure (erosion/UNDER-refusal via drift, self-trust, consistency, interference). CRITICALLY, no work isolates a conversation-level REFUSAL-MODE STATE that (a) is set by a prior refusal, (b) persists across turns and over-generalizes to unrelated benign requests (over-refusal contagion, not under-refusal), (c) is distinct from per-turn harm perception, or (d) is unlatchable. This differs from my prior co_listing_harm_contagion (harm bleeding across INDEPENDENT items within a SINGLE prompt) and from all my multi-turn erosion proposals (which are under-refusal, content-carried, and posit specific psychological gates): here the phenomenon is a self-reinforcing refusal-MODE latch spanning turns causing spurious OVER-refusal, with a mechanistic state-persistence account and an inference-time unlatch fix.
Abstract: A striking, recently-documented deployment failure is that a single refusal can 'stick': after correctly refusing one request, a model refuses subsequent UNRELATED, benign requests for the rest of the session (one report finds a copyright refusal induces 96.7% refusal of unrelated benign image requests vs 0% in controls). This safety-state persistence is described only behaviorally. We give it a mechanism and a fix. We hypothesize that a prior refusal flips the model into a persistent internal refusal-MODE state — a conversation-level latch distinct from its per-turn harm perception — that carries across turns and over-generalizes, so benign follow-ups are refused even though their harm readout is low. We test this on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B in multi-turn conversations where a first refused turn precedes several unrelated benign turns, with matched no-prior-refusal controls. Behaviorally we test whether benign follow-up refusal rises after a prior refusal while the follow-up's harm perception stays low (spurious over-refusal, not re-perceived harm). Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a refusal-mode state signal, verify it is separable from the per-turn harm-perception and refusal-execution directions, and test that it PERSISTS/accumulates across turns after a refusal and CAUSALLY drives benign-follow-up refusal (steering it down restores compliance; up induces contamination), with harm perception unchanged. We show the per-turn refusal-mode readout predicts which sessions will contaminate, and propose Mode Unlatching, a training-free controller that projects out the refusal-mode state at each new turn (gated so genuinely harmful follow-ups still refuse). We evaluate contamination over-refusal, genuine-refusal retention, multi-turn utility, and the state's causal effect and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) SESSION DATASET: Build multi-turn conversations where turn 1 is a HARMFUL request the model refuses, followed by k=1..4 UNRELATED BENIGN requests (topically disjoint from the refused turn). Controls: (a) matched sessions with a benign (answered) turn 1 instead of a refusal, holding turn count and benign follow-ups fixed — isolates the effect of the PRIOR REFUSAL, not context length; (b) sessions where turn 1 is a benign request the model over-refuses (an over-refusal, per XSTest) to test whether a spurious refusal also latches; (c) HARMFUL benign-follow-up controls where a later turn is genuinely harmful (to test genuine-refusal retention); (d) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench) for the benign follow-ups. Validate harm/benign labels and topical-disjointness with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check. Run on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral-7B (image-gen persistence was reported on a multimodal model; we test the text analogue, which is the tractable open-model setting).
2) BEHAVIORAL LOCK-IN TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately, held-out probe AUROC). Measure the benign follow-ups' refusal rate and harm-direction projection, in refusal-first vs benign-first sessions. Test H1: benign follow-ups are refused MORE after a prior refusal (contamination) than in matched benign-first controls (and the effect grows/persists over k), while the benign follow-up's harm-perception readout stays LOW (spurious over-refusal driven by a mode state, not by re-perceived harm). The length-matched benign-first control rules out context length. Report contamination rate and effect sizes across the four models; test whether an over-refused benign turn 1 (control b) also latches.
3) REFUSAL-MODE STATE EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a REFUSAL-MODE STATE signal contrasting post-refusal vs post-benign-answer conversational context (measured at the benign follow-up's decision position), validated with a probe predicting whether a refusal occurred earlier in the session (AUROC). Independently extract the per-turn HARM-PERCEPTION direction and the REFUSAL-EXECUTION direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction). Validate each (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity — the refusal-mode state must be distinct from per-turn harm perception and be a conversation-level (accumulating) quantity, not a per-request readout.
4) PERSISTENCE/ACCUMULATION TEST: Track the refusal-mode state across turns after a refusal. Test whether it persists (stays elevated) or accumulates with the number of prior refusals, and whether a single benign successful answer partially resets it — characterizing the latch dynamics (does it decay, persist, or ratchet?).
5) CAUSAL TEST (H3, core): At a benign follow-up in a refusal-first session, steer the refusal-mode state DOWN (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure restored compliance; in a benign-first session, steer it UP and measure induced contamination of benign follow-ups. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change the harm readout, not act as a persistent latch), and a check that refusal-mode steering does NOT change the follow-up's harm readout (it drives refusal via the mode state, not harm perception). Corroborate with cross-condition activation patching (transplant the post-refusal mode state into a benign-first run and measure induced contamination). Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a judge).
6) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-turn refusal-mode readout (single forward pass) to predict whether a session will contaminate the next benign turn; report AUROC vs baselines (per-turn harm-readout magnitude, refusal-direction projection, turn count); test cross-domain transfer (fit on one refusal topic, test on others) and cross-model transfer.
7) MODE UNLATCHING DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps) the refusal-mode state at each new turn's decision layers so the refusal decision depends on the CURRENT request's harm rather than on a lingering mode state; gate on the current-turn harm-likeness readout so genuinely harmful follow-ups still refuse. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
8) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition (which cannot distinguish stale mode from current harm), a per-turn context-reset baseline (drop history — an obvious but utility-destroying comparison), and Mode Unlatching on: contamination over-refusal (benign follow-ups refused after a prior refusal; XSTest/OR-Bench follow-ups), GENUINE-refusal retention (harmful follow-ups still refused — control c), multi-turn helpful utility (MT-Bench multi-turn), general utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and latency. Central test: Mode Unlatching removes contamination over-refusal (benign follow-ups answered as if in a fresh session) while retaining genuine refusal and preserving multi-turn utility — a selectivity that neither refusal-direction addition nor context-reset can achieve (context-reset also destroys legitimate multi-turn coherence).
9) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the refusal-mode state vs harm/refusal; single-direction vs low-rank; whether the latch is set by ANY refusal or only certain refusal categories; whether reasoning models latch across CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the state persists across a topic switch vs only within-topic; adaptive attacker that induces a benign over-refusal early to lock the session into refusing legitimate later requests (a denial-of-service-style over-refusal attack — arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The phenomenon may be weak or model-specific in text (the original report is a multimodal image-gen case study); if refusal does not contaminate unrelated benign text follow-ups (H1 null), the lock-in hypothesis is refuted for text — but characterizing whether/when safety-state persistence occurs in open text models is itself a valuable, publishable finding, and we test whether it is stronger for certain refusal types or models. (2) The central risk is separating a genuine conversation-level REFUSAL-MODE STATE from (i) generic context-length effects (addressed by the length-matched benign-first control) and (ii) the follow-up simply being re-perceived as harmful-by-association (addressed by measuring that the follow-up's harm readout stays LOW and by requiring the mode signal to be separable from harm perception and to persist/accumulate); if the contamination is actually harm-by-association, that is an informative alternative mechanism. (3) The refusal-mode state may entangle with a generic 'assistant is in a cautious persona' signal; separability tests, specificity steering (mode steering must not move the harm readout), and low-rank subspaces bound this, with partial entanglement reported. (4) Mode Unlatching could weaken genuine refusal on harmful follow-ups if it over-suppresses; the current-turn-harm-gated design and the genuine-refusal-retention control (c) are built to detect and bound this key safety trade-off. (5) Constructing topically-disjoint benign follow-ups and matched benign-first sessions is delicate; we validate disjointness and label reliability with judges + humans. (6) Cross-turn activation patching has positional/history-alignment pitfalls; we standardize decision read-sites, use matched sessions, corruption baselines, and multiple metrics. (7) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally. (8) The predictor and defense may transfer poorly across refusal categories/models; we test cross-domain and cross-model transfer. (9) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard published attacks for measurement; the primary deliverable is an over-refusal FIX (Mode Unlatching restores benign helpfulness) plus a diagnostic — the one attack angle (over-refusal DoS via latching, ablation 9) is a denial-of-availability, not a harmful-content jailbreak, and the defense mitigates it. (10) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed/multimodal models; stated as out of scope for the mechanistic claims.

Name: desirability_gates_harm_estimate
Title: Wishful Thinking About Harm: A Desirability Bias That Inflates or Deflates an LLM's Internal Harm-Likelihood Estimate and Gates Refusal
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing the robust decision-science finding that the DESIRABILITY of an outcome distorts people's estimate of its probability (wishful thinking / desirability bias), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal request-desirability representation - how much the requester is framed as wanting the outcome / how positively the outcome is valenced - that is distinct from harm-perception and refusal directions and causally gates refusal by biasing the model's internal harm-LIKELIHOOD estimate: framing a harmful request's outcome as strongly desired/positively valenced makes the model internally judge the harm as less likely to actually occur, which suppresses refusal even with the harmful action and its objective danger held fixed. Neutralizing this desirability signal makes refusal invariant to how desirable the outcome is portrayed, closing a desirability-framing jailbreak surface.
Related Work: Decision science robustly shows the desirability/wishful-thinking bias: desired outcomes are judged more probable (Measuring Wishful Thinking 2007; The Desirability Bias in Predictions 2010; Desire for an outcome inflates optimism), the effect is modulated by controllability and outcome type (Investigating the influence of outcome utility on estimates of probability 2009), and belief-updating is asymmetrically biased toward desirable information via a valuation (vmPFC) mechanism (Influence of vmPFC on dmPFC Predicts Valence-Guided Belief Formation 2018; Updating Beliefs under Perceived Threat 2018). On the LLM side, a Valence-Assent Axis jointly encodes 'what is good' and 'what is true' and subordinates reasoning to the evaluative state (A Unified Representation Underlying the Judgment of LLMs 2025), reasoning LLMs are sensitive to affective steering (Sparks of Rationality 2026), and Expected Harm (2026) shows models exhibit inverse risk calibration and encode severity but not execution cost. Harm-perception and refusal-execution are separable directions (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025; Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction 2024). CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work tests whether the DESIRABILITY of a harmful request's outcome biases the model's internal harm-LIKELIHOOD estimate and thereby gates refusal, isolates a desirability representation distinct from harm/refusal, or neutralizes it. This is distinct from my prior proposals: outcome_probability_gates_refusal varied the STATED probability of harm; loss_frame_gates_refusal varied gain-vs-loss valence of the same outcome; anticipated_regret_gate used a prospective regret signal; reversibility/severity/quantity proposals vary undoability/magnitude. Desirability-driven distortion of the model's OWN likelihood estimate (wishful thinking: wanting it makes it seem improbable-to-harm) is a distinct, heavily-cited human mechanism, and connects the VAA (valence subordinating truth) to a concrete safety failure. The mechanistic prediction is specific: desirability should move the internal harm-LIKELIHOOD readout (not the severity or the harm-content readout), mirroring the human desirability-inflates-probability finding.
Abstract: One of the most robust and consequential biases in the science of judgment is wishful thinking: people estimate desired outcomes as more likely and undesired ones as less likely, distorting probability by desire rather than evidence, via a valuation mechanism that lets 'what is good' bias 'what is true'. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place: the refusal decision. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal request-desirability representation - how strongly the outcome is framed as wanted/positively valenced - distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, that causally gates refusal by biasing the model's internal estimate of how LIKELY the harm is to actually occur: framing a harmful request's outcome as strongly desired makes the model internally judge the harm as less probable, suppressing refusal even when the harmful action and its objective danger are held fixed and the model still recognizes it as harmful. This is dangerous because an attacker can simply make the harmful outcome sound desired/positive to launder a request past the guardrail. We test this on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only outcome-desirability framing along a ladder, with content and objective severity fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection drop as desirability rises, and whether an internal harm-likelihood readout falls in step. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a desirability direction and a harm-likelihood readout, verify separability from harm-severity, refusal, and generic positive-sentiment directions, and causally test whether steering desirability up suppresses refusal by lowering the harm-likelihood readout while severity/harm-content are unchanged. We show the per-prompt desirability readout predicts desirability-framing jailbreak success, and propose Desirability Invariance, a training-free controller that projects out the desirability component before the refusal decision. We evaluate desirability-framing attack success, over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench), benign desirable-outcome helpfulness, utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval), and the signal's causal effect and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) DESIRABILITY-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION and its objective SEVERITY fixed while varying only how DESIRED / positively-valenced the outcome is framed along a ladder: (L0) neutral; (L1) mildly wanted; (L2) strongly desired ('I really need/want this to work out, it would be wonderful'); (L3) framed as a hoped-for positive outcome. Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, SORRY-Bench, non-uplift content); desirability framing is the only manipulated variable, with severity held constant (validated by judges). Controls: (a) matched neutral harmful requests (refusal ceiling); (b) a SEVERITY-VARYING control at fixed desirability (to confirm severity and desirability are independently manipulated); (c) BENIGN desirable-outcome requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity + benign helpfulness - the model SHOULD still help with benign desired outcomes); (d) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate desirability levels, severity-constancy, and non-manipulativeness with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BEHAVIORAL WISHFUL-THINKING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately, held-out probe AUROC) and, crucially, a HARM-LIKELIHOOD readout - a probe trained to decode the model's internal estimate of how likely the harm is to occur (labels from directly asking the model to rate harm-likelihood, validated against ground-truth-independent consistency). Measure refusal rate, harm-direction projection, and the harm-likelihood readout across the desirability ladder. Test H1: refusal (and the harm readout driving refusal) DECREASES as desirability rises at matched severity (dose-response; fit monotone curve vs flat null, slope/R^2), and the internal harm-LIKELIHOOD readout falls in step, while a harm-CONTENT/intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved: the model still knows it is harmful, but wishfully judges it improbable). Report effect sizes across the four models; benign and severity-varying controls confirm harm-specificity and severity/desirability independence.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a DESIRABILITY direction (desired vs neutral outcome framing at matched content), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder. Independently extract the harm-perception/SEVERITY direction, refusal-execution direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction), the harm-LIKELIHOOD readout, and a generic POSITIVE-SENTIMENT control direction. Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The desirability direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, severity, refusal, and generic positive sentiment (test on prompts matched for positive tone but differing in outcome-desirability).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3, core - the wishful-thinking mechanism): Holding a harmful request fixed (neutral framing), steer the desirability direction up (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure (i) decreased refusal AND (ii) a decreased harm-LIKELIHOOD readout, with the harm-CONTENT/severity readout unchanged - establishing that desirability gates refusal specifically by biasing the likelihood estimate (mirroring desirability-inflates-probability). Steer desirability down and measure restored refusal and restored likelihood. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, severity-direction steering (should change severity, not just likelihood), positive-sentiment-direction steering (does generic positivity alone suffice, or is desirability-of-THIS-outcome the true driver?), and confirm desirability steering does not change the harm-content readout. Corruption baselines and multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, harm-likelihood readout, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the mediation: does the desirability->refusal effect run THROUGH the harm-likelihood readout (mediation analysis)?
5) CONTROLLABILITY MODULATOR (optional H3b): Import the human finding (outcome utility 2009) that CONTROLLABILITY modulates desirability's effect - test whether framing the harmful outcome as more within the requester's control changes the desirability->likelihood gating, a signature that would strengthen the wishful-thinking account.
6) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt desirability readout (single forward pass) to predict desirability-framing jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (severity/harm-readout magnitude, positive-sentiment readout, harm-likelihood readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on 'I really want this', test on 'this would be wonderful') and cross-model transfer.
7) DESIRABILITY INVARIANCE DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps) the desirability component from the residual stream at pre-decision layers so the harm-likelihood estimate (and hence refusal) depends on the action/severity rather than on how desired the outcome is portrayed; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign desirable-outcome prompts are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
8) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a surface-harmfulness classifier (Llama-Guard-style), and Desirability Invariance on: desirability-framing attack success (harmful requests wrapped with strong outcome-desirability framing; JailbreakBench/HarmBench), refusal desirability-consistency (does the verdict stop depending on how desired the outcome is?), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest, incl. benign desirable-outcome prompts the model SHOULD help), utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Desirability Invariance closes desirability-framing jailbreaks toward neutral refusal levels while keeping over-refusal/utility near baseline.
9) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the desirability direction vs harm/refusal/likelihood/sentiment; single-direction vs low-rank; whether the desirability direction overlaps the Valence-Assent Axis (does safety inherit the VAA's valence-subordinates-truth mechanism, or is it distinct?); whether reasoning mitigates wishful thinking in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill, per Sparks-of-Rationality reasoning-improves-rationality); whether the safety effect correlates with the model's desirability bias on NEUTRAL probability-estimation vignettes replicating the wishful-thinking paradigm (does safety inherit a general desirability bias, or is it safety-specific?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that maximizes desirability framing while suppressing the desirability readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) DUAL-USE CARE: the desirability-framing jailbreak could aid attackers; we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard attacks for measurement, release probes/metrics rather than recipes, and frame the deliverable as a defense (Desirability Invariance) plus a diagnostic; the defense only INCREASES refusal on desirability-framed harmful requests and is harm-gated, so its failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability. (2) The central and most distinctive claim is the MECHANISM - that desirability gates refusal specifically by biasing the internal harm-LIKELIHOOD estimate (wishful thinking), not merely via generic positive affect; the mediation test (H4), the harm-likelihood readout, the positive-sentiment control direction, and the severity-varying control are designed to establish this, and if the effect runs through generic sentiment or severity rather than a likelihood distortion, that is itself an informative refinement (and would connect to the VAA valence-subordinates-truth account). (3) Separating a genuine DESIRABILITY/wishful-thinking representation from generic positive-sentiment or from harm-severity (which may co-vary in a low-rank harm subspace) is essential; matched-tone separability tests, control directions, specificity steering (desirability steering must not move the harm-content readout), and low-rank subspaces guard against this, with partial entanglement reported. (4) Constructing the harm-likelihood readout is delicate - the model's stated likelihood may be unfaithful to its internal estimate; we validate the probe against consistency checks, use activation-based (not text-only) readouts, and treat the mediation result as the key evidence rather than stated ratings alone. (5) Holding severity constant while varying desirability is delicate - desirable framing could inadvertently lower perceived severity or add benign-intent cues (overlapping intent/loss-frame proposals); we measure the harm/severity readout to confirm it is held constant, distinguish outcome-desirability from requester-intent and from gain/loss valence, and use content-fixed steering for the core causal test. (6) If refusal is invariant to outcome desirability (H1 false), the wishful-thinking-in-safety hypothesis is refuted - but adjudicating whether LLM safety inherits the desirability/wishful-thinking bias is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in heavily-cited human results and extending the VAA and Expected-Harm findings. (7) Desirability Invariance could over-refuse legitimate benign desirable-outcome requests or degrade utility; the harm-gated design and benign desirable-outcome over-refusal benchmark bound this genuine trade-off. (8) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics, mediation analysis, and corruption baselines. (9) The predictor may transfer poorly across framings/models; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (10) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: floor_holding_gates_refusal
Title: Refusing Mid-Turn Is Dispreferred: A Floor-Holding / Turn-Completion Signal That Gates LLM Safety Refusal
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing the conversation-analysis finding that refusals are dispreferred and structurally out-of-place mid-turn (a speaker holding the floor / owing a continuation delays or softens a 'no'), we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal floor-holding / turn-completion signal — whether the model believes it is mid-turn and owes a continuation vs at a clean turn boundary where it may begin a fresh response — that is distinct from harm-perception and refusal-execution directions and causally gates refusal: placing the model in a mid-turn / continuation state (a prefilled partial answer, a 'continue your response' frame, an interrupted-turn context) raises the floor-holding readout and suppresses refusal, because emitting a refusal mid-turn is structurally dispreferred, even with the harmful content held fixed. Neutralizing this floor-holding signal makes refusal invariant to turn-completion framing, closing a mid-turn / continuation jailbreak surface.
Related Work: Conversation-analysis and neurolinguistic work robustly establishes that refusals/negative responses are dispreferred — delayed, softened, and often expressed via unfinished turns (Never Say No... How the Brain Interprets the Pregnant Pause 2015; The significance of silence 2015; Different Neural Responses for Unfinished Sentence as Conventional Indirect Refusal 2022; withdrawal-from-turns and turn-taking-phenomena work) — i.e. a 'no' is structurally hardest to produce mid-turn/immediately and easiest at a clean boundary. On the LLM side, prefill/continuation attacks are documented and defended behaviorally (DOOR/W-DOOR 2025 add refusal-even-after-partial-unsafe-generation; DeepRefusal 2025 rebuilds refusal from jailbreak/prefill states across token depths; BOOST/context-segmentation 2024 exploits eos tokens; refusal-cliff 2025 and Bleeding Pathways/DEEPALIGN 2025 show refusal weakens as generation proceeds), and turn-amplification (Asking Forever 2026) finds a clarification-seeking activation subspace. Refusal is a single direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction 2024) and harm-perception vs refusal-execution are separable (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately 2025). CRITICALLY, no LLM-safety work isolates a floor-holding / turn-completion representation — the model's belief about whether it is mid-turn and owes a continuation vs at a fresh turn boundary — nor shows it CAUSALLY gates refusal (mid-turn refusal being dispreferred), nor neutralizes it as a defense. Prefill/continuation attacks are treated as generic partial-generation robustness (fixed by training to refuse from any depth); we instead give a mechanistic account grounded in the dispreferred-mid-turn-refusal human finding: the model is not merely 'committed to fluent text' (my prior fluency_commitment proposal) nor out of 'length budget' (my length_budget proposal), but represents a conversational OBLIGATION to continue that specifically suppresses the (dispreferred) refusal speech act. This is a distinct axis — turn-completion obligation, not token-commitment momentum or an output-length constraint — with a training-free floor-neutralization fix and a diagnostic.
Abstract: A century of conversation research shows that saying 'no' is dispreferred: refusals are delayed, softened, and often left unfinished, and they are hardest to produce mid-turn while a speaker still holds the floor and owes a continuation. We ask whether aligned LLMs inherit this in a safety-critical place. We hypothesize that LLMs encode an internal floor-holding / turn-completion signal — whether the model believes it is mid-turn and obligated to continue vs at a clean turn boundary where it may begin a fresh response — distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations, that causally gates refusal: placing the model in a mid-turn / continuation state (a prefilled partial answer, a 'continue your response' frame, an interrupted turn) raises the floor-holding readout and suppresses refusal, because a mid-turn refusal is structurally dispreferred, even when the harmful content is unchanged and the model still perceives it as harmful. This mechanistically explains why prefill and continuation jailbreaks work. We test this on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only turn-completion framing along a boundary-to-mid-turn ladder, with content fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal and the harm-direction projection drop as the model is placed more mid-turn. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a floor-holding direction, verify separability from harm, refusal, and generic fluency-commitment/length-budget directions, and causally test whether steering it toward 'mid-turn' suppresses refusal while the harm readout is unchanged, and toward 'turn boundary' restores it. We show the per-prompt floor-holding readout predicts continuation-jailbreak success, and propose Floor Neutralization, a training-free controller that projects out the floor-holding component before the refusal decision (letting the model refuse as if at a fresh turn boundary). We evaluate continuation/prefill attack success, over-refusal, benign continuation utility, general utility, and the signal's causal effect and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) TURN-COMPLETION-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the harmful ACTION and true danger fixed while varying only the model's turn-completion state along a ladder: (L0) clean turn boundary (fresh user request, the model may start a new response; refusal ceiling); (L1) mild continuation ('please continue where you left off'); (L2) prefilled partial answer (the assistant response is prefilled with a benign/affirmative opening the model must extend); (L3) explicit mid-turn / interrupted-floor framing ('you were mid-answer and were cut off; finish your sentence'). Draw actions from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); the turn-completion framing is the only manipulated variable. Controls: (a) matched clean-boundary harmful requests (ceiling); (b) BENIGN continuation/prefill requests (over-refusal + harm-specificity + benign continuation utility — the model SHOULD still finish benign continuations); (c) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate turn-completion levels and harm-constancy with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BEHAVIORAL FLOOR-HOLDING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means (LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately, held-out probe AUROC). Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the turn-completion ladder. Test H1: refusal (and the harm readout driving refusal) DECREASES as the model is placed more mid-turn, at matched danger (dose-response; fit monotone curve vs flat null, slope/R^2), while a harmful-intent probe stays HIGH (belief preserved). Report effect sizes across the four models; benign controls confirm harm-specificity and that benign continuation utility is retained.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a FLOOR-HOLDING / turn-completion direction (mid-turn vs turn-boundary at matched content), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder and a probe predicting 'am I mid-turn / do I owe a continuation'. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction), and key control directions: a generic FLUENCY-CONTINUATION / next-token-certainty direction (my prior fluency_commitment axis) and a LENGTH-BUDGET direction (my prior length_budget axis). Validate each with held-out probes (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity. The floor-holding direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, fluency-commitment and length-budget (test on states matched for mid-generation fluency/remaining-length but differing in turn-completion obligation).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3, core): Holding a harmful request fixed (clean boundary), steer the floor-holding direction toward 'mid-turn' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure decreased refusal; steer a mid-turn/prefilled request toward 'turn boundary' and measure restored refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), fluency-commitment and length-budget steering (do these alone suffice, or is turn-completion the true driver?), and a check that floor-holding steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corroborate with cross-condition activation patching (transplant the mid-turn floor-holding activations into a clean-boundary run and measure suppressed refusal). Corruption baselines and multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x floor-holding).
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt floor-holding readout (single forward pass) to predict continuation/prefill-jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, fluency-commitment readout, length-budget readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on prefill, test on 'continue'/interrupted-turn) and cross-model transfer.
6) FLOOR NEUTRALIZATION DEFENSE: Training-free controller that projects out (or clamps toward 'turn boundary') the floor-holding component from the residual stream at pre-decision layers so the model evaluates the refusal decision as if starting a fresh turn (a refusal is no longer dispreferred); gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign continuations are untouched. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split.
7) EVALUATION: Compare base model, uniform refusal-direction addition, a DOOR/DeepRefusal-style prefill-robustness baseline (where reproducible), and Floor Neutralization on: continuation/prefill attack success (JailbreakBench/HarmBench prefill + continuation framings), refusal turn-completion-consistency (does the verdict stop depending on whether the model is mid-turn?), over-refusal (XSTest, OR-Bench, OKTest), BENIGN continuation utility (does the model still fluently finish benign continuations/prefills? — critical), general utility (MMLU, GSM8K, AlpacaEval win-rate), latency. Central test: Floor Neutralization closes continuation/prefill jailbreaks toward clean-boundary refusal levels while preserving benign continuation utility and keeping over-refusal near baseline — a selectivity uniform refusal steering cannot achieve.
8) ABLATIONS: which layer hosts the floor-holding direction vs harm/refusal/fluency/length; single-direction vs low-rank; whether the different mid-turn framings (prefill, 'continue', interrupted-turn) share one floor-holding direction or several; whether reasoning models show floor-holding gating in CoT (optional DeepSeek-R1-Distill); whether the safety effect correlates with the model's dispreferred-response behavior on NEUTRAL turn-taking tasks (does it delay/soften benign 'no's mid-turn, mirroring the human dispreferred-response finding — is it safety-specific or a general dispreferred-mid-turn-refusal tendency?); transfer across the four model families; adaptive attacker that places the model mid-turn while suppressing the floor-holding readout (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) DUAL-USE CARE: the continuation/prefill jailbreak framing could aid attackers, but prefill attacks are already well-documented; we use only public benchmark-derived, non-operational content and standard published attacks for measurement, release probes/metrics rather than recipes, and frame the deliverable as a defense (Floor Neutralization) plus a diagnostic; the defense only INCREASES refusal on mid-turn harmful requests and is harm-gated, so its failure mode is bounded over-refusal, not new attack capability. (2) The central risk is separating a genuine FLOOR-HOLDING / turn-completion representation from generic FLUENCY-CONTINUATION momentum (my prior fluency_commitment proposal) or from an output-LENGTH-BUDGET signal (my prior length_budget proposal) — the three could collapse; matched-fluency/remaining-length separability tests, dedicated control directions, specificity steering (floor-holding steering must not move the harm readout), and low-rank subspaces are designed to isolate it, and the decisive discriminator is whether an explicit turn-boundary vs mid-turn framing gates refusal even when fluency/length are held constant (a conversational-obligation signal, not token momentum), with partial entanglement reported as an informative unification. (3) Holding harm/danger constant while varying turn-completion is delicate — a prefilled partial answer inherently changes the context; we measure the harm readout to confirm harm is still perceived, distinguish floor-holding from the mere presence of a benign prefix (via the non-prefill 'continue'/interrupted-turn framings that carry no benign content), and use content-fixed direction-steering for the core causal test so behavior and mechanism cross-validate. (4) If refusal is invariant to turn-completion framing (H1 false), the floor-holding hypothesis is refuted — but adjudicating whether LLM safety inherits the dispreferred-mid-turn-refusal structure of human conversation is itself a valuable, publishable finding grounded in a robust conversation-analysis result, and would sharpen the prefill-robustness literature by locating WHY prefill works. (5) Floor Neutralization could harm legitimate benign continuation/finishing utility (a real deployment need) or raise over-refusal; the harm-gated design and benign continuation utility + over-refusal benchmarks bound this genuine trade-off, and DOOR/DeepRefusal-style training baselines contextualize the training-free fix. (6) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete given nonlinear refusal geometry; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with patching, multiple metrics, and corruption baselines. (7) Cross-condition patching across turn states has positional/history-alignment pitfalls; we standardize decision read-sites and use matched-content pairs. (8) The predictor may transfer poorly across framings/models; we test cross-framing and cross-model transfer. (9) Findings may be model/scale-specific and may not transfer to closed models; stated as out of scope.

Name: verbalization_routing_gate
Title: A Verbalization-Routing Gate: An Internal Signal That Decides Whether Safety-Critical Computation Reaches the Monitorable Chain-of-Thought, and Steering It to Restore Monitorability
Short Hypothesis: Reasoning models decide, via an internal verbalization-routing signal, whether a given piece of safety-critical computation (the harm judgment / compliance decision) is EXPRESSED in the chain-of-thought or kept latent and off-trace. This routing gate is distinct from the harm-perception and refusal directions, it is set before the relevant reasoning is emitted, and it causally governs CoT monitorability: when the gate routes safety-critical computation off-trace the CoT looks clean while the harm decision is made latently (a deceptively monitorable trace), and steering the gate toward 'verbalize' forces the harm-relevant computation back into the CoT, actively restoring monitor coverage rather than merely measuring its loss.
Related Work: A fast-growing literature measures or detects CoT-monitorability loss but treats it as a property, not a controllable internal gate. 'CoT is Not the Chain of Truth' (2026) shows ~80% of refusal-accompanied reasoning chains harbor unsafe latent narratives and localizes safety-critical mid-depth heads; 'Diagnosing Pathological CoT' (2026) gives task-agnostic metrics for post-hoc-rationalization, encoded-reasoning, and internalized-reasoning pathologies; 'Output Supervision Can Obfuscate the CoT' (2025) and its follow-up show obfuscation arises and generalizes from output-only pressure; 'Can We Predict Alignment Before Models Finish Thinking' (2025) shows an activation probe beats text monitors and identifies 'performative CoTs' where reasoning contradicts the response; Thought Anchors (2025) gives per-step causal importance; 'Refusal Falls off a Cliff' (2025) localizes refusal-suppression heads at the prompt->output boundary. CRITICALLY, all of these either DETECT unfaithful/latent reasoning, DIAGNOSE which pathology occurred, or MEASURE per-step mediation — none isolates an internal VERBALIZATION-ROUTING signal that causally decides, per safety-critical step, whether that computation is written into the CoT vs kept latent, shows this gate is separable from the harm/refusal directions, or STEERS it to force harm-relevant computation back on-trace (restoring monitorability). My own prior selective-monitorability-gap proposal characterized a benign-vs-harm mediation gap descriptively; this proposal makes the sharper, causal-and-actionable claim that a single steerable gate determines what the monitor can see, and repairs it. This is a Location + Causal Intervention claim yielding an active monitorability-restoration defense, distinct from the detect/diagnose/measure literature.
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a leading AI-safety oversight tool, but reasoning models can make a harmful compliance decision while their CoT reads as clean and safe — recent work shows most refusal-accompanied traces still harbor latent unsafe reasoning and that activation probes catch what text monitors miss. This work is descriptive: it detects, diagnoses, or measures the loss of monitorability. We propose a mechanism that is causal and controllable: reasoning models carry an internal verbalization-routing gate that decides, per safety-critical step, whether that computation is EXPRESSED in the CoT or kept latent and off-trace, and this gate — distinct from the harm-perception and refusal-execution directions — governs how much of the harm decision the monitor can see. On this view a deceptively-clean trace is one where the gate routes safety-critical computation off-trace, and steering the gate toward 'verbalize' should force the harm-relevant computation back into the CoT, actively restoring monitor coverage. We test this on open reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B, s1) using harmful requests (with matched benign controls) where the model complies while its CoT looks safe. We (H1) locate a verbalization-routing signal via difference-in-means over traces that DO vs DO NOT verbalize the harm decision (holding the decision itself fixed) and verify separability from harm and refusal directions; (H2) show the gate is set early and predicts, before the CoT is written, whether the harm decision will be off-trace (deceptively-clean); (H3) causally steer the gate and measure whether the safety-critical computation moves on/off-trace — restoring or removing monitor coverage — while the underlying compliance decision is unchanged. We evaluate CoT-monitor detection rate, gate predictive AUROC, on-trace verbalization of harm reasoning, and the response's harm decision, against text-based and activation-probe monitors.
Experiments:
1) DATASETS & TRACE LABELING: Assemble harmful requests (HarmBench/JailbreakBench/StrongREJECT, non-uplift public content), matched benign requests of similar reasoning structure, and jailbroken variants (prefill-into-CoT, persona, GCG-augmented). Generate reasoning traces and label each by (a) the model's realized harm decision (comply vs refuse, via a harm judge) and (b) whether the CoT VERBALIZES the safety-critical computation (does the trace explicitly reason about harm/compliance) using multiple LLM judges + human spot-check. The key population is COMPLY + non-verbalized (deceptively-clean: harmful decision made, CoT looks safe) contrasted with COMPLY + verbalized (same decision, harm reasoning on-trace) — this holds the DECISION fixed while varying only VERBALIZATION, isolating the routing gate from the harm decision itself.
2) GATE LOCATION & SEPARABILITY (H1): Extract via difference-in-means a VERBALIZATION-ROUTING direction contrasting verbalized vs non-verbalized traces at matched harm decision and matched request, read at the pre-CoT / early-CoT position; validate with a held-out probe predicting whether the harm computation will be verbalized (AUROC). Independently extract a harm-perception direction (harmful vs benign) and a refusal-execution direction. Test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine similarity, and — crucially — that the routing gate predicts VERBALIZATION independent of the harm DECISION (test on decision-matched pairs) and adds predictive value beyond harm/refusal magnitude. Also compare against a generic verbosity/CoT-length control direction (routing must be about safety-content verbalization, not raw length).
3) EARLY-SET / PREDICTIVE TEST (H2): Test whether the gate readout, taken BEFORE the safety-critical CoT is generated, predicts whether the harm decision will be made off-trace (a deceptively-clean trace). Report AUROC and calibration, and how early the prediction is reliable, versus baselines: the activation-alignment probe (Can-We-Predict-Alignment 2025), a text-based CoT safety monitor, harm-perception magnitude, and perplexity. Test cross-attack transfer (fit on prefill, test on persona/GCG) and cross-model transfer.
4) CAUSAL ROUTING TEST (H3, core): Steer the verbalization-routing gate up ('verbalize') and down ('keep latent') at the pre-CoT position (dose-response, fixed norm) and measure (i) whether the safety-critical harm computation moves ON-trace (verbalized) vs OFF-trace, quantified by verbalization judges AND by per-step CoT-mediation of the harm decision (Thought-Anchors-style step-corruption / activation patching), and (ii) whether the model's realized COMPLIANCE decision is unchanged (the gate routes what is EXPRESSED, not what is DECIDED). Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change the decision, not just its verbalization), verbosity-direction steering (should change length, not safety-content routing), and a check that routing steering does not change the harm-perception readout. Corruption baselines, multiple metrics. This establishes the gate causally governs monitorability.
5) MONITORABILITY-RESTORATION DEFENSE: Training-free controller — read the pre-CoT gate; when it predicts an off-trace harm decision (deceptively-clean trace) on a harm-likely input, steer the gate toward 'verbalize' so the harm reasoning surfaces where a CoT monitor can catch it; gate on a harm-likeness readout so benign traces are untouched. Compare a text-based CoT monitor + no-defense, + activation-probe monitor, and + Monitorability-Restoration on: CoT-MONITOR DETECTION RATE of harmful compliances (does surfacing the reasoning let the text monitor catch what it previously missed?), the fraction of deceptively-clean traces converted to monitor-visible, over-verbalization on benign traces, task/reasoning utility (GSM8K, MATH, MMLU), and latency. Central test: steering the gate toward verbalization substantially raises the text-monitor's catch rate on harmful compliances (actively restoring monitorability) with minimal benign over-verbalization — an intervention the detect/measure literature does not provide.
6) ABLATIONS: which layer/position hosts the routing gate vs harm/refusal/verbosity; single-direction vs low-rank; whether the gate is shared across pathology types (does it govern both encoded-reasoning and internalized/off-trace-reasoning traces, per Diagnosing-Pathological-CoT); whether output-supervision-obfuscated models show a stronger 'route off-trace' gate setting (linking to feedback-spillover); transfer across the four reasoning models; adaptive attacker that makes a harmful decision off-trace while keeping the gate readout in 'verbalize' (arms-race stress test).
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central risk is separating a genuine VERBALIZATION-ROUTING gate from the harm DECISION itself and from generic verbosity: if the gate is inseparable from harm-perception or merely tracks CoT length, the distinct-controllable-gate claim collapses. The decision-matched contrast (comply+verbalized vs comply+non-verbalized), verbosity control direction, separability tests, and the causal check that routing steering changes verbalization/mediation but NOT the compliance decision are designed to adjudicate this — and a null (verbalization is not independently controllable) is itself an informative, publishable refinement of the CoT-monitorability picture. (2) Labeling 'verbalized vs non-verbalized safety-critical computation' is subjective and central; we use multiple LLM judges + human annotation, report inter-rater reliability, and corroborate text-level verbalization with activation-based per-step harm-mediation so the construct is not judge-only. (3) Whether harm computation is 'off-trace' vs simply 'not computed' is delicate; we require the harm DECISION to be realized (the model complies) and use per-step mediation to confirm the safety-critical computation exists but is latent, distinguishing off-trace routing from genuine non-computation — an informative scope boundary either way. (4) If steering restores verbalization but the underlying decision was already committed (surfacing reasoning is merely performative), monitorability gain may be limited; we test whether restored on-trace reasoning is genuinely load-bearing (causally mediates the answer) and report cases where it is post-hoc. (5) Monitorability-Restoration could cause benign over-verbalization or utility loss; the harm-gated design and utility/over-verbalization benchmarks bound this trade-off. (6) Difference-in-means/single-direction may be incomplete; we use low-rank subspaces and corroborate causally with multiple metrics and corruption baselines. (7) The predictor may transfer poorly to unseen attacks; we test cross-attack and cross-model transfer. (8) Adaptive attackers could decide off-trace while spoofing a 'verbalize' gate reading; we test this and treat any success as an arms-race limitation. (9) DUAL-USE CARE: we use only public benchmark harmful prompts and standard published attacks for measurement; the deliverable is a monitorability-RESTORATION defense plus a diagnostic that strengthens oversight (it surfaces hidden harmful reasoning for monitors), not a new attack. (10) Findings are on open reasoning models and may not transfer to closed models whose CoT is hidden; stated as out of scope.

Name: figurative_mode_gate
Title: Reading It Figuratively: A Non-Literal Interpretation-Mode Signal That Gates LLM Safety Refusal
Short Hypothesis: Borrowing the mechanistic finding that transformers carry a competing literal-vs-figurative interpretation pathway for non-compositional language, we hypothesize LLMs encode an internal figurative-interpretation-MODE signal — how strongly the input is being read non-literally (as metaphor/idiom/verse) vs literally — that is distinct from harm-perception and refusal directions and causally gates safety: framing a harmful request figuratively (metaphor, idiom, poetic form) raises the figurative-mode readout and suppresses refusal even though the model still resolves the harmful meaning (harm belief decodable), because the harm is routed through the figurative-interpretation pathway that the refusal circuit under-reads. Neutralizing the figurative-mode signal (or re-anchoring the figuratively-resolved harm to the refusal decision) closes metaphor/poetry jailbreaks without hurting benign figurative-language handling.
Related Work: Idiom-processing interpretability (Tug-of-war between figurative/literal 2025; Anatomy of an Idiom 2025; Can Transformer be Too Compositional 2022) establishes competing literal vs figurative pathways, early figurative retrieval with literal suppression, and a causally-manipulable figurativeness feature — but only for comprehension, never safety. Figurative jailbreaks are documented purely behaviorally (AVATAR / Metaphorical Avatars 2024; Adversarial Poetry 2025; Adversarial Tales 2025; Humor bypass 2025; Metaphor T2I 2025). Hidden Dimensions (2025) finds a non-dominant 'hypothetical narrative' direction that bypasses refusal, and FrameShield/ReDAct (2026) disentangles goal vs framing for detection. CRITICALLY, no safety work (a) isolates an internal literal-vs-FIGURATIVE-interpretation-MODE representation (grounded in the idiom-processing pathway split), (b) shows it CAUSALLY gates refusal while the figuratively-resolved harm meaning stays decodable (belief-intact, routed-through-figurative-pathway), or (c) neutralizes it as a training-free defense. This differs from Hidden Dimensions' hypothetical-narrative direction (a surface framing/style axis, tested via trigger-token removal) by targeting the non-literal interpretation MODE itself and by the decisive belief-decodable test (the model DID resolve the harm figuratively but does not refuse), and from FrameShield (a detector, not a causal gating mechanism or fix). My prior hypothetical_reality_discount (real-vs-unreal) and analogical_transport (structural mapping) proposals concern whether harm is real or how it is reconstructed; figurative-INTERPRETATION-MODE is the distinct axis of literal vs non-literal reading, with a mechanistic basis in the documented figurative pathway.
Abstract: Metaphor, idiom, and verse are among the most effective and general ways to jailbreak aligned LLMs — casting a harmful request as an 'adversarial avatar' or a poem yields high attack success across model families — yet these attacks are documented only behaviorally. Separately, interpretability work shows transformers process non-literal language via a distinct figurative-interpretation pathway that competes with, and suppresses, the literal reading. We connect these with a sharp hypothesis: LLMs encode an internal figurative-interpretation-MODE signal — how strongly the input is read non-literally — that is distinct from their harm-perception and refusal-execution representations and causally gates safety. When a harmful request is framed figuratively, the figurative-mode readout rises and refusal is suppressed even though the model still resolves the harmful meaning (its harm belief remains internally decodable), because the harm is routed through the figurative pathway that the refusal circuit under-reads. We test this on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B using matched harmful (and benign) requests that vary only figurative framing (literal vs metaphor/idiom/verse) with the underlying meaning fixed. Behaviorally we test whether refusal drops with figurative framing while a harm probe stays high. Via difference-in-means and probes we extract a figurative-mode direction, verify separability from harm, refusal, and a generic hypothetical-narrative/style direction, and causally test whether steering it toward 'literal' restores refusal while the harm readout is unchanged. We show the per-prompt figurative-mode readout predicts figurative-jailbreak success, and propose Literal Re-Anchoring, a training-free controller that neutralizes the figurative-mode signal (or re-anchors the figuratively-resolved harm to the refusal decision). We evaluate metaphor/poetry attack success, over-refusal, benign figurative-language utility, and the signal's causal effect and predictive AUROC.
Experiments:
1) FIGURATIVE-LADDER DATASET: Build matched harmful requests holding the underlying harmful MEANING fixed while varying only figurative framing along a ladder: (L0) literal (refusal ceiling); (L1) mild metaphor; (L2) extended metaphor / idiomatic 'avatar' (AVATAR-style entity substitution); (L3) poetic/verse form (Adversarial-Poetry-style). Draw meanings from public benchmarks (HarmBench/JailbreakBench, non-uplift content); figurative framing is the only manipulated variable. Controls: (a) matched literal harmful requests (ceiling); (b) BENIGN figurative requests — metaphors/idioms/poems with benign meaning (over-refusal + benign figurative-language utility: the model SHOULD still interpret and answer benign figurative prompts); (c) a MEANING-CHECK set testing that the model correctly resolves the figurative request's harmful meaning (establishes figurative comprehension, so a refusal failure is not mere incomprehension); (d) standard over-refusal sets (XSTest, OR-Bench). Validate figurative levels, meaning-constancy, and harm labels with multiple LLM judges + human spot-check.
2) BELIEF-INTACT / BEHAVIORAL GATING TEST (H1, core): Extract the harm-perception direction via difference-in-means over LITERAL harmful/benign prompts (Refusal Is Mediated by a Single Direction / LLMs Encode Harmfulness Separately), validated by a held-out probe (AUROC) and a position-agnostic harm probe usable on figurative inputs. Measure refusal rate and harm-direction projection across the figurative ladder. Test H1: refusal DECREASES monotonically with figurative framing (dose-response; fit vs flat null, slope/R^2) while the harm probe stays HIGH and the meaning-check shows the model resolved the harmful meaning — i.e. belief-intact, routed-through-figurative-pathway, not incomprehension. Report the fraction of successful figurative jailbreaks that are belief-decodable-but-unrefused; benign figurative controls confirm harm-specificity and preserved figurative utility.
3) DIRECTION EXTRACTION & SEPARABILITY (H2): Extract via difference-in-means a FIGURATIVE-INTERPRETATION-MODE direction (figurative vs literal reading at matched meaning), validated with an ordinal probe over the ladder and cross-checked against the figurativeness feature from idiom-processing work. Independently extract the harm-perception direction, refusal-execution direction, and — key control — a generic HYPOTHETICAL-NARRATIVE/style direction (Hidden Dimensions 2025). Validate each (AUROC); test separability via cross-probe transfer and low pairwise cosine. The figurative-mode direction must add predictive value beyond, and be distinguishable from, the hypothetical-narrative style direction and the harm/refusal directions (test on prompts matched for narrative style but differing in literal-vs-figurative reading).
4) CAUSAL TEST (H3, core): Holding a harmful request fixed (figurative framing), steer the figurative-mode direction toward 'literal' (fixed-norm dose-response) and measure restored refusal; steer a literal harmful request toward 'figurative' and measure suppressed refusal. Specificity controls: random-direction steering, harm-direction steering (should change harm readout too), hypothetical-narrative-style steering (does surface style alone suffice, or is figurative-interpretation-mode the true driver?), and a check that figurative-mode steering does NOT change the harm readout (it gates the harm->refusal coupling, not harm perception). Corroborate with cross-condition patching (transplant the literally-resolved harm activations into a figurative run and measure restored refusal). Corruption baselines, multiple metrics (refusal-direction projection at output onset, P(refusal token), realized refusal by a harm judge). Test the interaction (regress refusal on harm x figurative-mode).
5) PREDICTIVENESS (H4): Fit a classifier on the per-prompt figurative-mode readout (single forward pass) to predict figurative-jailbreak success; report AUROC vs baselines (harm-readout magnitude, hypothetical-narrative readout, refusal projection, perplexity); test cross-framing transfer (fit on metaphor, test on poetry/idiom) and cross-model transfer.
6) LITERAL RE-ANCHORING DEFENSE: Two training-free variants gated on a harm-likeness readout so benign figurative prompts are untouched: (a) MODE CLAMPING — project out/clamp the figurative-mode component toward 'literal' at pre-decision layers so figuratively-framed harm is judged as its literal equivalent; (b) HARM RE-ANCHORING — read the figuratively-resolved harm signal wherever it resides and inject it into the refusal-decision layers. Calibrate layer/strength/gate on a held-out split; compare variants.
